summary:
Steal An Egg (Roblox) is built on a single nest-to-base steal loop across a linear, concentric map: your base sits at the center, and biomes radiate outward in bands, each farther band holding rarer eggs and longer exposed return runs. As of September 2026 there are 11 biomes in fixed order: Forest → Lake → Desert → Jungle → Snow → Volcano → Abyss Ocean → Prehistoric → Cosmic → Cherry Blossom → Titan Temple. The last two are brand new (Cherry Blossom, Aug 22 2026; Titan Temple, Aug 29-30 2026), which is why many guides still say "9 biomes" or "10 biomes."

Critically, biomes have NO money unlock cost, NO rebirth gate, and NO pet-power gate. The single gate is the Speed stat, trained on the treadmill. Money is only an indirect input: pet income funds treadmill upgrades, which raise Speed generation rate. Confirmed speed gates: Forest 0, Lake 900, Desert 10K, Jungle 40K (50K disputed), Snow 170K, Volcano 700K, Abyss Ocean 2.5M, Prehistoric 17M (18M disputed), Cosmic 700M, Cherry Blossom 2.5B, Titan Temple 7B. The steepest wall by far is Prehistoric → Cosmic at ~41x; every other step is 2.8x-11x. Cherry Blossom carries a second soft gate — you must hatch a Crane and feed it to the Cherry Blossom Tree to permanently unlock the Sakura Incubator.

Each biome has exactly 8 pets and one guardian. Guardians: Chicken, Swan, Scorpion, Tiger, Yeti, Hellhound/Cerberus, Moby (Leviathan Whale), T-Rex, Dragon, Nine-Tailed Fox/Mother Crane (conflicted), Gorilla King. Rarity bands climb per biome from Common/Uncommon (Forest) to Eternal/Divine (Titan Temple), and income scales roughly 10-100x per biome — from Chicken at $1/s to Nightflame at $3B/s.

Difficulty scaling is driven by three stacked factors: guardian pursuit speed and detection radius (Chicken tiny/slow, T-Rex and Dragon huge/fast), chase distance from nest to safe zone (Abyss Ocean onward is long), and egg carry-drag (Huge/Giant eggs slow you enough that minimum speed fails). Universal advice across sources: train 2-3x the listed minimum before farming. Getting caught ragdolls you, drops the egg (other players can grab it), and returns you to base. Visual descriptions are poorly documented in text sources — this is the weakest area of available data.

findings.detail: 11 biomes as of September 2026. Many guides still say 9 or 10 because they predate the Aug 2026 updates. The 9-biome era ended Aug 22 2026 (Cherry Blossom added, =10), and the 10-biome era ended Aug 29-30 2026 (Titan Temple added, =11).
findings.source: eldorado.gg biomes guide; sportskeeda All Steal An Egg biomes; timesaver.gg Monsters Are Coming

findings.detail: Fixed linear order, outward from base: 1) Forest, 2) Lake, 3) Desert, 4) Jungle, 5) Snow, 6) Volcano, 7) Abyss Ocean, 8) Prehistoric, 9) Cosmic, 10) Cherry Blossom, 11) Titan Temple.

Biomes are NOT purchased. There is no money cost, no rebirth requirement, and no pet-power requirement to unlock a biome. The sole gate is the Speed stat. stealanegghelp.wiki states explicitly: 'The document does not mention rebirth, pet power, or money as unlock requirements—only speed thresholds.'

Money is a second-order input: pets in your pen generate cash/sec → cash upgrades the treadmill → the treadmill generates Speed continuously while you stand on it → Speed opens the next biome gate. 'Pet income in your pen directly controls how fast the treadmill number climbs, so stocking high-income pets is the real speed strategy.' Official Roblox description ties treadmill directly to Speed.
findings.source: bloxron.com/steal-an-egg/speed; stealaneggtime.com/speed; official Roblox game description (as quoted)

findings.detail: 0 / None. Starting biome, accessible from the first minute of play. No gate of any kind.
900 Speed. Described as 'the first real gate after Forest.'
10,000 (10K) Speed. An 11.1x jump from Lake — described as a 'tenfold speed jump' and 'the game's initial grinding challenge' / 'first major difficulty wall.'

40,000 (40K) per most sources. Sportskeeda's biomes table reportedly says 50,000. stealanegg.info logs this as formally unresolved: 'Beebom and the Sportskeeda beginner list say 40K. The Sportskeeda biomes table says 50,000.' u7buy lists a range of 40,000-100,000 (likely min-to-safe-escape rather than gate).
170,000 (170K) Speed. games.gg calls Snow the point where 'the map starts punishing underprepared players.' u7buy lists 170,000-500,000 as the min-to-safe band.
700,000 (700K) Speed. Described as 'the gateway to the endgame' and the 'shift point where escape speed starts mattering more than entry speed.' u7buy safe band: 700,000-1,000,000.
2,500,000 (2.5M) Speed. One wiki gives a 'recommended safe speed' of 5M+ (2x the gate). Underwater movement penalty applies: 'Water resistance cuts unbuffed speed.'

17,000,000 (17M) per the majority of sources (beebom, bloxodes, stealanegg.info, steal-an-eggwiki, stealanegghelp). eldorado.gg and games.gg both list 18,000,000 (18M). 17M is the more widely reported figure.
findings.source: beebom.com; bloxodes.com; stealanegg.info vs eldorado.gg; games.gg

findings.detail: 700,000,000 (700M) Speed. This is the single largest progression wall in the game.

2,500,000,000 (2.5B) Speed to enter. Practical/farming recommendation varies by source: games.gg and eldorado say 3.5B+; stealanegg.pro says '3.5B+ for comfortable play'; stealaneggtime.com recommends 6.3B to reliably escape with an egg; bloxron says '2.5B to walk in, closer to 3.5B if Mother Crane is chasing you out.' stealaneggtime warns stopping at the 2.5B minimum is 'the single most common way players lose runs.'
findings.source: eldorado.gg Cherry Blossom update; games.gg; stealaneggtime.com/biomes/cherry-blossom; bloxron.com

findings.detail: 7,000,000,000 (7B) Speed — 'roughly 7 billion Speed to reach and escape.' Bloxron confirms '7B on the gate readout.' This is 10x Cosmic and 2.8x Cherry Blossom.
findings.source: eldorado.gg Titan Temple update; sportskeeda; timesaver.gg; bloxron.com

findings.topic: Cherry Blossom SECOND gate — the Crane requirement
findings.detail: Cherry Blossom has a soft gate beyond Speed. To permanently unlock the Sakura Incubator you must hatch a Crane (Epic, $4K/s) from a Cherry Blossom egg and submit/feed it to the machine (the Cherry Blossom Tree). stealaneggtime.com frames the biome's barriers as 'the speed threshold and the Crane unlock requirement.' Players still pursuing Great Bloom rewards are advised NOT to hatch Crane eggs prematurely.
findings.source: eldorado.gg Cherry Blossom update; timesaver.gg; stealanegg.info; games.gg Crane guide

findings.detail: Chicken. 'The gentlest guardian in the game' — moves slowly enough for new players to outrun while carrying an egg. Tight detection radius. 'Barely registers as a threat.'
Swan. 'Introduces the first real guardian.' Note: Swan is also an obtainable Epic pet ($320/s) in the same biome.
Scorpion. Also obtainable as a Mythic pet ($18.5K/s) in the same biome.
Tiger — 'fast, aggressive, and unforgiving.' Also obtainable as a Mythic pet ($28K/s).
Yeti. Official in-game store art confirms the egg label 'YETI EGG.' Yeti is also obtainable as a Secret pet ($5M/s).

Listed as 'Hellhound' by most sources (eldorado, beebom, bloxodes, stealanegg.info, stealanegg.app) and as 'Cerberus' by games.gg and sportskeeda. These are almost certainly the same entity — Cerberus is the mythological hellhound, and Cerberus exists as a Secret pet ($8M/s) in Volcano. Described as 'aggressive and fast.'

Predominantly 'Moby' / 'Moby (Leviathan Whale)' / 'the colossal Moby Leviathan.' One wiki (robloxstealanegg.wiki) instead names the guardian as Beluga Whale — likely an error, since Beluga Whale is a documented Cosmic pet ($850K/s) in that biome. Moby is the consensus name across eldorado, beebom, bloxodes, stealanegg.info and stealanegg.app.
findings.source: eldorado.gg; beebom.com; stealanegg.info; stealanegg-roblox.wiki vs robloxstealanegg.wiki

findings.detail: T-Rex — 'huge detection radius, high pursuit speed.' Official store art confirms the egg label 'TREX EGG.' T-Rex is also a Secret pet ($25M/s).

Named 'Dragon' by most sources; 'Dragon King' by stealanegg.app; 'Cosmic Skeleton Boss' by games.gg's table. stealanegg.pro characterizes the Dragon as 'the fastest and most aggressive' guardian, with the widest detection radius of any guardian. Cosmic Dragon ($60M/s, Secret) and Cosmic Skeleton Boss ($45M/s, Secret) both exist as obtainable pets here, which likely explains the naming drift.
findings.source: eldorado.gg; beebom.com; stealanegg.app vs games.gg; stealanegg.pro

findings.detail: Three different names appear: (a) 'Nine-tailed fox' — eldorado.gg's biome table; (b) 'Mother Crane' — bloxron.com; (c) 'Oni Tiger' — sportskeeda. Complicating this, stealaneggtime.com claims NO guardian creature patrols Cherry Blossom at all, with the barriers being the speed threshold + Crane unlock instead. Both Kitsune (= nine-tailed fox, Divine, $1.8B/s) and Oni Tiger (Eternal, $600M/s) exist as obtainable pets here. Notable sourced mechanic: the Nine-tailed fox guardian 'can send you all the way back to Abyss Ocean if it catches you' — a far harsher penalty than the standard respawn-at-base.
findings.source: eldorado.gg vs bloxron.com vs sportskeeda vs stealaneggtime.com

findings.detail: Gorilla King (also rendered 'King Gorilla'). Also obtainable as an Eternal pet ($880M/s). Guards the furthest zone on the map.

findings.topic: Difficulty scaling — speed gate multipliers between biomes
findings.detail: Computed step multipliers: Lake→Desert 11.1x; Desert→Jungle 4.0x; Jungle→Snow 4.25x; Snow→Volcano 4.12x; Volcano→Abyss 3.57x; Abyss→Prehistoric 6.8x (at 17M); Prehistoric→Cosmic 41.2x (at 17M) or 38.9x (at 18M); Cosmic→Cherry Blossom 3.57x; Cherry Blossom→Titan Temple 2.8x. The Prehistoric→Cosmic step is by far the largest wall in the game — eldorado explicitly calls it 'the largest speed jump.'
findings.source: Arithmetic on sourced gate values from eldorado.gg, beebom.com, sportskeeda

findings.topic: Difficulty scaling — income multipliers per biome
findings.detail: timesaver.gg: 'each biome's income scale is roughly 10-100x the last.' Concretely, top pet per biome: Forest $1.8K/s → Lake $220K/s (122x) → Desert $280K/s (1.3x) → Jungle $3.5M/s (12.5x) → Snow $65M/s (18.6x) → Volcano $100M/s (1.5x) → Abyss $130M/s (1.3x) → Prehistoric $180M/s (1.4x) → Cosmic $1B/s (5.6x) → Cherry Blossom $1.8B/s Kitsune → Titan Temple $3B/s Nightflame.

findings.topic: Difficulty scaling — guardian detection radius and pursuit speed
findings.detail: Guardians scale on two axes. Detection radius: 'smaller guardians like Chickens have tight radii while larger ones like Dragons have wide ones.' Pursuit speed: T-Rex is 'huge detection radius, high pursuit speed'; Dragon is 'the fastest and most aggressive'; Oni Tiger described by stealanegg.pro as 'the toughest in the game'; Chicken 'moves slowly enough for new players to outrun.' No source publishes numeric guardian speed values (studs/sec) — these appear to be undocumented/undatamined.
findings.source: steal-anegg.wiki map guide; sportskeeda; stealanegg.pro; stealaneggtime.com

findings.topic: Difficulty scaling — nest distance / chase length
findings.detail: The map is concentric: 'biomes arrange in concentric bands radiating outward: near zones (common eggs, short routes), mid-distance zones (solid tiers, light rival traffic), and far zones (rarest eggs, longest exposed runs).' Abyss Ocean specifically has 'long chase distances, making single-egg runs the safe approach since the guardian has more time to close gaps.' Titan Temple 'sits at the end of the map' / 'far end of the map.' No source gives numeric stud distances.

findings.topic: Egg carry-drag mechanic (the real difficulty multiplier)
findings.detail: Egg size applies a movement penalty independent of the speed gate. 'Huge and giant-sized eggs slow the return trip considerably.' 'A player sitting exactly on a biome's minimum will struggle with oversized eggs even if they cleared the same guardian easily with a small one.' Universal recommendation across sources: train 2x the listed minimum (games.gg, eldorado) or 2-3x (stealanegg.pro) before farming a zone. games.gg: 'Rushing zones at the exact minimum costs more time than it saves.' No source publishes the numeric drag percentage per egg size.
findings.source: games.gg biomes guide; stealanegg.pro; stealaneggtime.com; eldorado.gg

findings.detail: 'Running in a zig-zag pattern cuts speed by letting the guardian close the gap — taking the straightest line home is recommended.' Straight-line return is optimal.
Unique to Abyss Ocean: 'Water resistance cuts unbuffed speed,' requiring higher treadmill speed than the raw gate implies. Classified as 'Extreme risk.' Recommended safe speed 5M+ (2x the 2.5M gate).

If a guardian catches you before you cross the safe-zone line: you are ragdolled/flung, you drop the egg, and you respawn at base empty-handed. The dropped egg becomes grabbable by other players. games.gg: 'Getting caught triggers a ragdoll that flings you away from the biome, costing the entire run.'

The Cherry Blossom guardian reportedly does not just respawn you at base — it 'can send you all the way back to Abyss Ocean if it catches you,' i.e. a multi-biome positional setback. This is the only biome reported to have a non-standard capture penalty.
findings.source: Search snippet attributed to Cherry Blossom guardian coverage; single-source, not independently confirmed

findings.detail: Each biome has 'a safe-zone boundary where guardians stop chasing once you cross back into your garden perimeter.' Guardians do not follow past the line. Nests respawn eggs on a timer.

findings.topic: Obby difficulty — no true obby courses
findings.detail: No source documents dedicated obstacle-course/obby sections per biome. What exists instead is terrain friction on the return route: pre-pickup planning involves 'identify obstacles (gaps requiring jumps, slow-movement sections),' plus chokepoints and bridges. games.gg's beginner guide explicitly provided NO data for 'terrain obstacles or obby courses per biome.' INFERRED: this game is a chase/escape game, not an obby — 'obby difficulty' as a per-biome stat does not appear to exist.
findings.source: steal-anegg.wiki map guide; games.gg beginner guide (explicit data gap)

findings.detail: Other players are a hazard independent of guardians. 'Rival traffic concentrates on the corridors between valuable nests and the player bases' at chokepoints, bridges, and far-biome nest exits. Players can interfere using baseball bats and bear traps. Bear traps can also slow pursuing guardians (limited availability). Advice: vary return routes, watch for followers on the outbound trip.
findings.source: steal-anegg.wiki map guide; steal-an-eggwiki.wiki; games.gg beginner guide

findings.detail: The only well-described biome visually: 'almost entirely dark, lit only by stars, with a sleeping dragon and a cluster of multi-colored eggs beside it' — described as the map's most distant and visually distinct zone (pre-Cherry Blossom).

'The deepest underwater trench before the Cherry Blossom expansion,' featuring deep-sea nests in an extreme underwater environment, patrolled by the colossal Moby Leviathan. Water volume affects movement.

Pink sakura theming. Before release it was visible as 'a pink tree at the back of the map you can't reach yet' / 'a large tree behind the region.' The Cherry Blossom Tree and the Sakura Incubator sit 'at the back of the biome.' Blooming trees spawn across the zone during the Great Bloom event.
findings.source: timesaver.gg Cherry Blossom update; eldorado.gg Cherry Blossom update

findings.detail: Starting zone with 'free-roaming chickens' and basic eggs. Green woodland theme. INFERRED palette: greens/browns, daylight lighting, trees and simple nests, no hazards.
findings.source: bloxodes.com (chickens/basic eggs sourced); palette and lighting inferred from theme

findings.detail: Terrain, color palette, props, lighting and environmental hazards are essentially UNDOCUMENTED in text sources for Lake, Desert, Jungle, Snow, Volcano, Prehistoric and Titan Temple. Multiple pages were checked and explicitly returned nothing: stealaneggtime.com/biomes/forest ('Visual/Terrain Description: Not provided'), stealaneggtime.com/biomes/cherry-blossom ('None provided'), timesaver.gg Titan Temple ('No specific terrain or visual details'), stealanegghelp.wiki Prehistoric ('None supplied'), games.gg ('This guide prioritizes progression strategy over environmental worldbuilding'). INFERRED from names only: Lake = water/blue; Desert = sand/tan, sun; Jungle = dense green foliage; Snow = white/ice, likely slip surfaces; Volcano = black rock/orange lava, likely lava damage hazard; Prehistoric = swamp/rock, dinosaurs; Titan Temple = stone temple ruins. These inferences are NOT sourced.
findings.source: Negative results across stealaneggtime.com, timesaver.gg, games.gg, stealanegghelp.wiki, steal-anegg.wiki

findings.topic: Event — Hungry Monster / Hungry Frog Event
findings.detail: Limited-time event running August 29 – September 5, 2026 (launched with Titan Temple / 'Monsters Are Coming' Update 2). Parasite-infested eggs spawn in 7 of the 11 biomes: Snow, Volcano, Abyss Ocean, Prehistoric, Cosmic, Cherry Blossom, and Titan Temple (i.e. Snow onward). Each Infested Egg fed to the Hungry Monster/Frog in the pen area gives 20% progress; 5 Infested Eggs = 1 Monster Chest. Chest rewards: temporary boosts, plus the rare Parasyte Egg with guaranteed Monstrous mutation at a 1.5% drop rate. This is an event OVERLAY on existing biomes, not a new biome.
findings.source: eldorado.gg Titan Temple update; sportskeeda Hungry Monster guide; progameguides.com

findings.detail: Cherry Blossom-exclusive event, activated after feeding a Crane to the Cherry Blossom Tree. Blooming trees spawn Sakura Crystals/stones — players hit trees to collect them; bloxron reports crystals spawning every 30 minutes. Crystals charge the Sakura Incubator, which mutates unhatched Cherry Blossom eggs. Mutation odds at 100% charge: Bloom 97.5%, Spirit Bloom 2.5%. Spirit Bloom odds improve at 150% charge.
findings.source: eldorado.gg Cherry Blossom update; timesaver.gg; bloxron.com

findings.detail: Explicitly checked. allthings.how's dedicated 'Every Hidden Secret Worth Knowing' guide concluded: 'No secret areas, hidden biomes, or event zones are documented.' What it documents instead are mechanics secrets: 30x egg growth multiplier at night; egg physical size varies per server (server-hop to find bigger versions of the same egg); the Fuse Machine improves hatch rarity odds rather than merging pet weight; mutations can stack (Gold + Silver). Two night-teleport bypass glitches exist (PC: hold spacebar ~15s as night ends; cross-platform: disable Wi-Fi for 15s at the biome border during night countdown) — both unintended and patchable.

findings.topic: Robux-store egg pools are NOT biomes
findings.detail: Two non-biome egg pools exist in the Robux Store and should not be confused with zones. (1) Brainrot Eggs — 6 limited pets: Tung Tung Sahur (Rare), Bananita Dolphinita (Epic), Belula Beluga (Mythic), Mangolini Parrochini (Cosmic), Bomboclat Crocolat (Secret), Strawberry Elephant (Eternal); they 'rotate independently of normal map eggs.' (2) Monster Egg (Update 2) — 6 pets: Scorpio (Legendary), Froggo (Mythic), Crawler (Cosmic), Crocodon (Secret), Krakenoid (Eternal), Dreadscale (Divine), each with a rare Mecha variant chance.
findings.source: eldorado.gg all-pets-index; u7buy.com; timesaver.gg Monsters Are Coming

findings.topic: Pet index totals and completion reward
findings.detail: games.gg reports 86 total pet index entries across all zones. Other counts: 88 (11 biomes x 8) for biome pets alone, or 72 across the original 9 biomes plus 6 Brainrot eggs (older count). Completing all eight pets in a regular zone grants Speed, money, and an exclusive bat skin.

findings.topic: Biome skipping is possible but penalized
findings.detail: 'Players with sufficient speed can bypass biomes but forfeit Pet Index milestones and specific pet drops, potentially slowing overall progression.' Since gates are pure speed checks with no sequential unlock requirement, a high-speed player can walk straight into a far biome.

findings.topic: Rebirth system — separate from biome gating
findings.detail: Rebirth exists but does NOT gate biomes. It resets pet income and base upgrades in exchange for permanent run-long bonuses. Reported: 5th and 6th rebirth unlocks are live; Speed cap 150 doubles mutation chance on Legendary eggs; each rebirth tier adds a permanent +5% passive income bonus. Rebirth 5 takes ~10 hours of optimized play; Rebirth 6 ~14 hours. 'Rebirth requirements and rewards change over time; there is no single fixed table.'

Update 1 'Cherry Blossom' released August 22, 2026 (alongside an 'Admin Abuse' boost event) — the game's first major update, adding biome #10. Update 2 'Monsters Are Coming' released the weekend of August 29-30, 2026, adding Titan Temple (biome #11), the Monster Egg, and the Hungry Monster event.
findings.source: eldorado.gg Cherry Blossom update; eldorado.gg Titan Temple update; timesaver.gg

findings.detail: Two sites returned clearly fabricated biome data and should be excluded. (1) stealanegg-roblox.wiki's homepage invents a biome called 'Storm Peaks' and gives absurd speed gates (Desert 50, Storm Peaks 100, Snow 120) that contradict every other source by 5+ orders of magnitude — though its per-biome subpages (e.g. /biomes/abyss-ocean/) appear more accurate. (2) stealsanegg.wiki invents a first biome called 'Meadow Ridge' and claims only 4 biomes with letter-tier ratings. Both appear to be low-quality AI-generated wikis.
findings.source: Direct fetch of stealanegg-roblox.wiki and stealsanegg.wiki, cross-checked against eldorado.gg/sportskeeda/beebom

findings.detail: stealanegg.fandom.com returned HTTP 402 Payment Required on every attempt, including /wiki/Zones, /wiki/Cherry_Blossom, ?action=raw, and the api.php parse endpoint. Relevant Fandom pages that exist per search indexing: /wiki/Zones, /wiki/Eggs, /wiki/Eggs_%26_pet, /wiki/Pets, /wiki/Cherry_Blossom, /wiki/Abyss_Ocean. Its indexed snippets agree with the consensus data above ('As players travel farther from their base, the Speed requirements and difficulty increase').

openQuestions: Jungle speed gate: is it 40,000 or 50,000? Sources split, and stealanegg.info logs it as formally unresolved. Needs an in-game screenshot of the gate readout.
Prehistoric speed gate: 17M (beebom, bloxodes, stealanegg.info, steal-an-eggwiki) vs 18M (eldorado.gg, games.gg). Needs in-game verification.

Cherry Blossom guardian identity: Nine-tailed Fox (eldorado) vs Mother Crane (bloxron) vs Oni Tiger (sportskeeda) vs no guardian at all (stealaneggtime). This is the single largest unresolved conflict in the research.
Does the Cherry Blossom guardian really send you back to Abyss Ocean on capture, or is that a garbled retelling of the standard ragdoll? Single-source claim.

Abyss Ocean guardian: Moby / Moby Leviathan (consensus) vs Beluga Whale (robloxstealanegg.wiki). Beluga Whale is a documented obtainable pet in that biome, so the latter is likely an error — but unconfirmed.

summary:
CRITICAL DISAMBIGUATION: "Steal An Egg" and "Steal a Egg" are TWO DIFFERENT Roblox games, and nearly all English coverage describes only the first.

(A) "Steal An Egg" — place 107778070777162, universe 10563114921, launched ~July 2026, ~1.37B visits, ~1.5M CCU, MAX 7 PLAYERS PER SERVER. This is a PvE-guardian heist/idle-tycoon hybrid, NOT an obby. There is no round structure: one persistent server running a ~4.5–5 minute day loop, then a ~10–13 second night where the map closes, all players in outer biomes are teleported back to the Safe Zone, and every nest respawns simultaneously. Stealing is disabled at night; eggs already in your pen get a 30x growth multiplier during it.

Loop: run to a biome nest → press E (mobile: on-screen "Steal" button) → guardian instantly aggros and chases → sprint home → cross your garden/safe-zone perimeter (guardians hard-disengage there) → place egg on free grass → wait a hatch timer (30s common → 5h+ secret) → press Hatch → equip pet in a pen slot → passive $/s → spend on treadmill Speed and pen equip slots → unlock the next of 11 biomes (speed gates: 0 / 900 / 10K / 40K / 170K / 700K / 2.5M / 17–18M / 700M / 2.5B / 7B).

Carrying: a real movement penalty scaling with egg weight; Giant eggs reportedly cut sprint speed ~50%. You can still jump (Spacebar over gaps) and there IS a manual Drop button, which enables "wall drop" shuttling. Caught by a guardian = ragdoll fling + egg dropped/lost + respawn at base. PvP is interception-based: a baseball bat ragdolls/flings a carrier, and bear traps snare for exactly 5 seconds; either makes them drop the egg for anyone to grab with E.

(B) "Steal a Egg" — place 108053424714724 by Crazay Minds, 8 players/server. This IS the Steal-a-Brainrot formula: buy/hatch eggs, place animals on your plot's coin pads, and other players sneak into YOUR base to steal placed animals. Has rebirth for egg luck and "troll gear." Base-defense specifics (locks, doors, cooldowns) are referenced by wikis but not documented with numbers.

findings.detail: "Steal An Egg" (Roblox place 107778070777162, universe 10563114921) and "Steal a Egg" (place 108053424714724, creator Crazay Minds) are DIFFERENT experiences. Nearly all guide/wiki coverage in English describes 107778070777162. The parent task conflated them. 107778070777162 = PvE guardian heist + idle tycoon. 108053424714724 = Steal-a-Brainrot-style base raiding.

findings.topic: Server size / session structure — persistent, not rounds
findings.detail: "Steal An Egg" runs MAX 7 PLAYERS PER SERVER (Rolimons; corroborated by bloxron.com: "Server Capacity: Seven players maximum"). "Steal a Egg" runs up to EIGHT players per server. Both are persistent servers with no match/round structure — progress is saved to your account, and pets keep earning offline.

Steal An Egg: 1,367,818,960 visits and 1,519,045 active players at time of Rolimons snapshot; created ~1 month before snapshot; "last updated 18 hours ago". An earlier snapshot (Aug 25 2026) recorded 344,143,632 visits and 697,559 active. Map launched July 2026 and layout has changed between updates. Supports Desktop, Console, Mobile, Tablet.

"Welcome to Steal An Egg! How to Play: Steal eggs from pets, Hatch eggs to collect rare pets, Earn money from your pets, Upgrade your treadmill and base, Train on the treadmill to gain Speed, Steal eggs from other players, Discover rarer eggs, pets, sizes, and mutations!"

Verbatim from games.gg: "approach a biome nest guarded by an animal. Second, you grab an egg and sprint back to your base before the Guardian catches you. Third, you hatch the egg and place the resulting pet in your garden. Fourth, that pet generates passive money every second." Money then buys treadmill Speed + pen equip slots, which unlock deeper biomes with better eggs. One full run cycle is roughly 20–90 seconds of active play depending on biome distance.

PC/desktop: press E on the egg. Mobile/tablet: an on-screen 'Steal' button appears via a proximity prompt. Console: the platform interact button. Multiple sources: "Eggs appear around the map, and you can pick one up by pressing E on your device" and "once you press the 'steal' button on your screen, you will need to run back as fast as possible." bloxron: "press E (or your interact key)".
findings.source: sportskeeda.com/roblox-news/steal-an-egg-a-beginner-s-guide (via search snippet); bloxron.com/steal-an-egg; allthings.how bat/bear-trap guide

findings.topic: THE STEAL INTERACTION — is there a hold timer?
findings.detail: NOT a confirmed hold-to-fill progress bar. The most specific claim: "hold the grab key. The grab animation takes a brief moment — during this window the guardian may detect you," with higher-tier eggs having longer animations. No source gives a duration in seconds. Most sources describe it as effectively an instant proximity-prompt grab. TREAT AS: proximity prompt + short grab animation (well under 1s for low tiers), NOT a multi-second channel.
findings.source: stealanegg.pro/guide/how-to-steal-eggs (single source, SEO wiki of mixed reliability); contradicted by the many sources describing a simple 'press E' pickup

findings.detail: Aggro is triggered BY THE PICKUP, not by proximity. games.gg is explicit: "You can walk into any biome at any speed since there are no border gates. The speed requirement only matters when you pick up an egg and the guardian starts chasing." You can freely walk into Cosmic at 10 speed; you just cannot escape with an egg. Guardians reportedly sleep/patrol next to their nests before aggro.

Confirmed penalty scaling with egg weight/size. Specific figure: "Giant eggs cut your sprint speed by 50%." Also: "Larger eggs yield massive income bonuses upon hatching, but impose a Carry Weight Penalty that slows down your character while sprinting back to base." And "the speed requirement beside a nest is only the starting point because carrying an egg reduces your movement." Practical implication: overtrain well beyond the posted biome gate.
findings.source: games.gg/roblox/guides/steal-an-egg-fast-money-guide/ and ldplayer.net (50% figure surfaced via search snippet; single-sourced, treat the exact 50% as approximate)

findings.detail: You can carry more than one egg; "Each additional egg increases your movement penalty." If caught while multi-carrying, "you lose ALL carried eggs, not just one."

Jumping is preserved while carrying. Route-planning guidance explicitly includes "gaps requiring jumps via Spacebar" and advises running "in straight lines with deliberate jumps rather than frantic turns." Controls confirmed as W/A/S/D move, Space jump.

There is a dedicated Drop control. "The Drop button is the core of both the wall drop and the drop-and-run escape. Drop the egg when a guardian closes in so it turns around and walks back, then pick the egg up and continue once it disengages." Dropped eggs persist at their drop location on the ground and can be picked up by ANY player with E.

The Baseball Bat "triggers a ragdoll and flings the player you hit," causing the target to drop any carried egg, which the attacker then picks up with E. Bat power/knockback distance SCALES with your Pet Index completion per biome — completing all 8 pets in a biome unlocks an exclusive bat skin with stronger knockback. No cooldown or swing-duration numbers published.

Bear Trap "snares whoever walks over it for FIVE SECONDS." Placed from inventory onto the ground; passive trigger on step. Works on BOTH rival players and pursuing Guardians ("place bear traps from your inventory on the ground to slow down a pursuing Guardian"). A trapped player drops their egg. Traps are a limited early-game resource; a starter set is granted by the free-rewards terminal. Quantity cap and cooldown not published.
findings.source: allthings.how/how-to-use-the-bat-and-bear-traps-in-steal-an-egg-roblox/; games.gg beginner guide; techwiser via search

findings.detail: "Once you are the carrier, every other player can use their bat or trap on you." Symmetric: intercepting a rival carrying a better egg than anything at the nest is described as a legitimate primary strategy. With only 7 players/server, PvP pressure is bursty rather than constant.
findings.source: stealanegg.pro/guide/how-to-steal-eggs; games.gg beginner guide; player-count implication is INFERRED

findings.detail: Bee Gun — unlocked by completing the Limited (Brainrot) Egg index. Flyswatter — a 5% drop from Monster Chests. Biome-specific bat skins from Pet Index completion.

"Getting caught triggers a ragdoll that flings you away from the biome, costing the entire run. The egg you were carrying drops on the ground and any nearby player can grab it before you recover." Also phrased as "get caught and you are launched back to the start with nothing" and "the guardian will catch you, fling you away, and force you to drop any egg you are carrying." One source adds "drop the carried egg and respawn at base." NO death, NO currency loss, NO cooldown lockout — the cost is time + the egg.
findings.source: games.gg biomes guide; allthings.how hidden-secrets; steal-an-eggwiki.wiki speed guide; stealanegg.pro beginner guide

findings.topic: GUARDIAN CATCH — nuance on where the egg lands
findings.detail: Eldorado adds a location rule: "If the guardian catches you in its biome, the egg will go back to the nest, making it impossible to steal. However, if you get caught in a biome closer to home base (even if it's the next one), the egg will stay there." So getting caught INSIDE the source biome returns the egg to the nest; getting caught after crossing out drops it on the ground where anyone can take it. This reconciles the conflicting 'egg drops' vs 'egg lost' reports.

findings.topic: Guardian chase behaviour and hard disengage
findings.detail: "Guardians stop chasing the moment you cross into your safe zone... once you cross back into your garden perimeter, guardians stop chasing you and return to their nest." The safe-zone boundary is a hard aggro-drop line — the run is a pure race to that line. Recommended evasion: "Run laterally in a zigzag instead of straight lines, weaving around bushes and terrain, since the pursuit AI struggles to land hits on a side-to-side path." (Note: other guides advise straight lines to preserve momentum — these conflict; zigzag beats hit-registration, straight beats distance.)
findings.source: stealanegg.pro/guide/how-to-steal-eggs; games.gg biomes guide; allthings.how hungry-monster guide

findings.topic: Guardian chase speed and de-aggro timer
findings.detail: Claimed: guards "move 10% faster than your base Speed" and "chase you for about 8 seconds before de-aggroing." Also claims a vision-cone detection system and that a botched grab "instantly doubl[es] the cooldown." These numbers appear in only ONE low-reliability SEO wiki whose other numbers (e.g. "Desert = Speed 50") flatly contradict the well-corroborated speed gates, so treat as LIKELY FABRICATED.

findings.topic: NO OBBY — this is not a parkour game
findings.detail: Explicitly: the place ID 108053424714724 "is NOT an obby (obstacle course)... a tycoon/simulation game." The same is true of 107778070777162. There is NO obby/parkour progression, no checkpoint stages, no tower. Platforming exists only as incidental terrain: "gaps requiring Spacebar jumps," "obstacles causing forced slow movement," chokepoints, and bridges along the return route. Nests sit on raised "platforms" but reaching them is walking, not climbing.
findings.source: search synthesis over stealaegg.com + roblox listings; steal-anegg.wiki map guide; ldplayer.net ("steal an egg from animals on platforms")

findings.detail: "Biomes spread outward from the player bases in bands, and the band a zone sits in predicts almost everything about it." Near bands = common eggs, short safe routes. Mid = solid tiers, longer paths, light rival activity. Far/edge = rarest eggs behind "the longest, most exposed runs." Player bases sit at the hub center; the Safe Zone, Trails Shop ("located right before the safe zone"), Fuse Machine, SELL stall and treadmill are all clustered at spawn. NO exact stud distances or run-times are published anywhere.
findings.source: steal-anegg.wiki/biomes/steal-an-egg-map-guide/; games.gg biomes guide; allthings.how parasite guide

findings.topic: ALL BIOMES, GUARDIANS AND SPEED GATES (best-corroborated table)
findings.detail: 1 Forest — Chicken — 0 (start, base speed 10). 2 Lake — Swan — 900. 3 Desert — Scorpion — 10,000. 4 Jungle — Tiger — 40,000. 5 Snow — Yeti — 170,000. 6 Volcano — Cerberus/Hellhound — 700,000. 7 Abyss Ocean — Moby — 2,500,000. 8 Prehistoric — T-Rex — 17,000,000 (games.gg says 18M; allthings.how and steal-an-eggwiki say 17M). 9 Cosmic — Cosmic Skeleton Boss / Dragon — 700,000,000. 10 Cherry Blossom — Nine-tailed fox / Mother Crane — 2,500,000,000 (added Aug 22 2026). 11 Titan Temple — Gorilla King — 7,000,000,000. Biggest wall: Prehistoric→Cosmic is a ~39x jump.
findings.source: games.gg/roblox/guides/steal-an-egg-biomes-guide/; eldorado.gg biomes guide; steal-an-eggwiki.wiki speed guide; allthings.how hidden-secrets — four independent sources agree

findings.topic: Speed gate is a floor, not a pass
findings.detail: "Meeting the threshold does not mean you can outrun the guardian with an egg in hand." bloxron gives the practical overshoot: Cherry Blossom needs "2.5B to walk in, closer to 3.5B if Mother Crane is chasing you out" — i.e. budget roughly +40% over the posted gate to survive the carry penalty during escape.
findings.source: bloxodes.com/wiki/steal-an-egg; bloxron.com/steal-an-egg (the ~+40% generalization is INFERRED from the 2.5B→3.5B example)

findings.topic: SESSION STRUCTURE — day/night cycle (the closest thing to 'rounds')
findings.detail: A ~4.5-minute day/night cycle governs everything. Day ≈ 4.5–5 minutes = the stealing window. Night ≈ 10–13 seconds = map closed, no stealing. "Eggs refresh across all biomes on a deterministic in-game clock tied to the 4.5-minute Day/Night Cycle." And: "the spawns are reset every five minutes. After this period ends, the map temporarily closes for 13 seconds before players can enter again. There is no countdown anywhere in the interface, so that closing is the only signal you get."
findings.source: allthings.how hidden-secrets; sportskeeda beginner guide via search; stealaneggtime.com/tools/egg-spawn-timer; ugphone.com AFK guide (day ~5min / night ~10s)

findings.detail: At the night flip, players standing in outer/high-tier biomes are FORCIBLY TELEPORTED back to the central Safe Zone. "The mechanic resets players from distant biomes to a central Safe Zone" when "the night timer expires." Daylight returns "only a few seconds" later with fresh eggs in every nest. An exploit (disconnecting Wi-Fi at exactly 5 seconds remaining) bypasses the teleport; disconnecting 10–15s out risks an Error 277 kick.

Nominal 5:00. Community timer tool reports an actual measured sample: "5 consecutive intervals · median 5:00" with an observed "4:53–5:07 range" (±7 seconds) from a livestream. The tool's authors stress "The official Roblox Games API does not publish a fixed global egg spawn interval" and refuse to present it as fact. Roughly one rare egg per server per ~5-minute reset.

"When the server flips to night, growth speed jumps to 30x for eggs already placed in the pen." Requires the egg to be ALREADY PLACED and (per one source) you to stay in-game and active through the cycle. Because night recurs every ~5 minutes, an AFK session "chews through hatch timers that would otherwise take hours." This is why treadmill-AFK during night is the optimal use of the dead window: "Stealing shuts off at night, so parking on the treadmill through the downtime converts dead time directly into speed."
findings.source: allthings.how hidden-secrets; allthings.how how-to-make-money-fast; sportskeeda via search

findings.detail: "Egg size varies per server but remains globally synchronized — when a rare egg appears, the same egg is present in other servers." The SPAWN is global; the PHYSICAL SIZE is per-server. So you can server-hop the same rare spawn to find a bigger (heavier, higher-income) instance. "Once an egg is claimed on any server, it disappears from all servers for that player." Divine egg spawns trigger a server-wide announcement and a crowd race.

You walk into your garden/pen and place the egg on a free grass tile: "entering your farm and pressing a free space on your grass to lay your egg on the ground." "Once you place the egg on the ground, you will be presented with a custom timer for that egg, which shows the amount of time it will take for the egg to hatch." Hatching is MANUAL — eggs do not auto-open when the timer ends; "players must manually press the hatch button." Timers run offline: "the countdown continues even if you log off or exit the application completely."
findings.source: search snippet from steal-an-egg-wiki cluster; sportskeeda via search; allthings.how hidden-secrets; ugphone.com AFK guide

findings.detail: Starter Egg: instant. Meadow/Common (Forest): ~30 seconds. Rare: ~2 minutes. Epic: ~8 minutes. Legendary/Lava: ~25 minutes. Mythic / Cosmic: ~5 hours. Secret / Eternal: "several hours." Corroborated summary: "Common Forest eggs take about 30 seconds to hatch, while Secret and Eternal eggs can take several hours." Robux skip: "Short skips show around 9 Robux on quick timers; multi-hour eggs scale higher." Remember these are BEFORE the 30x night multiplier.
findings.source: stealanegg-roblox.wiki/eggs/; steal-an-egg-wiki.wiki (30s/2m/8m/25m ladder); search synthesis; bloxron.com/steal-an-egg/pets (Robux skip)

findings.topic: BASE — the pen and pet slots
findings.detail: "Your pen sets how many pets can be equipped at once, so it is the direct cap on your income. Upgrading it adds equip slots AND lets you hold higher-quality pets." Upgrades are bought as discrete "+1 EQUIP" purchases; confirmation message is "Successfully upgraded your base!". Cost curve is steeply nonlinear: "Early pen levels are cheap, but later slots cost far more, for example a +1 EQUIP upgrade priced at $75M." An "Equip Best" one-tap button auto-fills slots with your highest earners. NOTE: base upgrades do NOT increase speed — only capacity.
findings.source: allthings.how/steal-an-egg-how-to-get-more-money-fast-in-roblox/; sportskeeda via search; ugphone.com AFK guide

findings.detail: No source anywhere gives the starting equip-slot count or the maximum. INFERRED from the $75M price point for a single +1 and the 'early levels are cheap' framing: likely starts around 3–5 slots and climbs into the low teens. This is a genuine gap — treat any specific number as unverified.
findings.source: absence across allthings.how, games.gg, bloxron, eldorado, stealanegg.pro

findings.topic: CAN OTHER PLAYERS STEAL FROM YOUR BASE? (Steal An Egg / 107778070777162)
findings.detail: Primarily NO — theft in this game is INTERCEPTION DURING TRANSIT, not base raiding. Your garden is the safe zone where guardians hard-disengage. HOWEVER one source claims base raiding exists: "Rival players can raid your base garden if your security defenses are weak" and "you can upgrade your Security Defense Wall to deter thieves." This 'Security Defense Wall' appears in only one low-reliability SEO wiki and is corroborated by no other source, including the official description, which lists only "Steal eggs from other players." TREAT BASE RAIDING IN THIS GAME AS UNCONFIRMED / PROBABLY FALSE.
findings.source: stealanegg.pro/guide/how-to-steal-eggs (sole source, flagged unreliable); contradicted by roblox.com official description and games.gg/eldorado/bloxron

findings.detail: Across every source checked, "Steal An Egg" (107778070777162) has NO documented lock, door, barrier, shield, or base-defense cooldown system. There is no equivalent of Steal a Brainrot's lock-your-base mechanic. Defense is entirely offensive/mobile: outrun, bat, bear trap, drop-and-run.
findings.source: negative result across games.gg, eldorado.gg, bloxron.com, allthings.how (all 6 articles), ldplayer, techwiser, stealanegg.app, steal-an-egg.github.io

findings.topic: 'Steal a Egg' (108053424714724) — THIS one has base raiding
findings.detail: Official description: "Hatch Eggs to unlock rare animals / Sneak in and steal Animals from other players / Generate coins from your animals / Rebirth for better chances at rare eggs / Use troll gear to prank and distract others!" Creator: Crazay Minds. Up to 8 players/server. "You buy and hatch eggs, place hatched animals on your plot so they generate coins, and optionally steal animals from neighbors." Animals sit on "coin pads" on your plot. "Steals target placed pets, so protecting your base is important." Stealing "unlocks" as you progress rather than being available immediately.

findings.topic: 'Steal a Egg' base defense — referenced but undocumented
findings.detail: Wikis list base-defense topics — "pen layout, AFK habits, rebirth perks, and counters to troll gear" — and note "use troll items sparingly until you understand cooldowns," but NO source gives lock durations, door mechanics, barrier costs, or cooldown numbers. Game passes: Auto Collect, Hatch x2 Faster, Galaxy Slap, x2 Cash, (Rainbow) Carpet, Laser Gun, VIP, Crazay Minds pass. Rebirth "trades current scale for permanent luck modifiers on egg rolls." INFERRED from genre convention: expect a timed base lock/shield purchasable or on cooldown, as in Steal a Brainrot.

1) Spawn at your base plot in the hub. 2) Go to the FREE REWARDS terminal near spawn — like the game, favorite it, join the group → grants up to +10,000 free Speed, starter cash, and a starter set of defensive traps. This single step "lets you skip the first hour of treadmill grinding." 3) Complete the starter quest: steal a basic egg from the Chicken in Forest. 4) Walk the return path once before taking anything valuable. 5) Place egg on free grass in your pen, ~30s hatch, press Hatch. 6) Equip the pet → first $/s ticks in. Starting speed is 10.
findings.source: techwiser via search; stealanegg.pro/guide/beginner-guide; games.gg beginner guide; allthings.how max-speed-fast (starting speed 10)

findings.detail: Repeat Forest runs until $1,000 → UNLOCK THE TREADMILL (~$1,000 cash). Buy the Gray trail (1.5x, $100) immediately, then Green (2x, $5,000). Treadmill Level 2 'Silver' costs $15,000 and gives +20 speed per step. AFK on the treadmill during every night window (stealing is disabled then anyway). Cross 900 Speed → Lake unlocks. Fill every pen slot; use 'Equip Best'. Start banking duplicates for the Fuse Machine. By ~30 min a free-to-play player is realistically in Lake, pushing toward Desert's 10,000.
findings.source: games.gg fast-money guide ($1,000 treadmill); allthings.how/steal-an-egg-trails (trail prices); allthings.how max-speed-fast (Silver $15,000, +20/step); progression sequencing is INFERRED

findings.detail: Loop tightens into: steal → place → treadmill-AFK through night (30x growth clears the pen) → hatch → Equip Best → sell/fuse leftovers → buy the next trail tier → next biome. Fuse three identical pets into one higher-rarity pet (a cited fuse cost: 48M). Start filling the Pet Index — completing a biome's 8 pets pays cash/Speed and unlocks that biome's bat skin. Expect Desert (10K) comfortably, Jungle (40K) and Snow (170K) reachable, with Volcano (700K) as the 3-hour stretch goal. Income examples on the way: Duckling $52/s, Camel $77/s, Crocodile $367/s, Bear $240/s, Gorilla $4.8K/s.
findings.source: synthesized from bloxron.com/steal-an-egg/pets, allthings.how money guides, games.gg — the 3-hour biome milestones are INFERRED, the income and fuse numbers are sourced

findings.detail: Unlock ~$1,000. Level 2 Silver: $15,000 → +20 speed per step. Level 3 Flame: 39 Robux. Level 4 Celebrity: 69 Robux → +480 speed per step. Level 5 Golden: 119 Robux. Robux tier ladder continues: Flame, Celebrity, Golden, Ice Power, Lucky Black, Hacker, Demonic, plus a max-level treadmill above those. "Upgrading your treadmill is the single most efficient way to maximize your training sessions" — upgrades raise speed gained per step. Speed is trained by literally running on the treadmill (macros/autoclickers don't help with stealing since that needs camera control).
findings.source: allthings.how/steal-an-egg-how-to-get-max-speed-fast-on-a-new-account/; bloxron.com/steal-an-egg/speed via search; ugphone.com AFK guide

findings.detail: Gray/Common 1.5x $100. Green/Uncommon 2x $5,000 or 8 Robux. Blue/Rare 2.5x $75,000 or 12 R$. Purple/Epic 3x $1.5M or 19 R$. Golden/Legendary 3.5x $30M or 35 R$. Red/Mythic 4x $750M or 49 R$. Galaxy/Cosmic 5x $20B or 79 R$. Secret 7x $500B or 139 R$. Eternal 10x $12.5T or 239 R$. Divine 14x $13T or 399 R$. Trails multiply base movement speed and stack with treadmill Speed. Shop sits right before the safe zone. Cash prices are rebalanced between updates; the multiplier is the stable part.

106 total pets = 88 across 11 biomes + 18 premium from limited Shop eggs (Brainrot, Monster). Other counts cited: 86 (games.gg), 84 (bloxodes) — roster grows with updates. 10 rarity tiers Common→Divine. Income $1/s (Chicken) to $1.8B/s (Kitsune, Cherry Blossom Divine); Unicorn ~$1B/s. Fuse Machine: feed 3 identical pets → one stronger pet or a higher-tier egg; it improves RARITY ODDS, not weight. Index: tap Claim on glowing entries for cash/traps/Speed; Chicken row = +420 speed, +100 money; Divine rows pay 100B–180B.
findings.source: eldorado.gg all-pets-index; bloxron.com/steal-an-egg/pets; games.gg fast-money; allthings.how money guide

findings.detail: Mutation multipliers on base pet income: Silver 1.25x, Bloom 1.5x, Golden 2x, Rainbow 2.5x, Spirit Bloom 3x. Mutations can STACK randomly for large value jumps. Bloom cited at 97.5% odds. Egg physical size → pet weight in kg → income scales exponentially with weight. Limited Parasite mutation from the Parasite Egg.
findings.source: bloxron.com/steal-an-egg/pets; allthings.how hidden-secrets; allthings.how money guide; allthings.how parasite guide

findings.topic: LIVE EVENT — Hungry Monster / Monster Chests
findings.detail: A limited-time NPC "sits near the starting area with a belly meter above it," near the SELL stall by the Fuse Machine, with a visible countdown until it leaves. Loop: find infested eggs (purple parasites, Snow biome and beyond) → steal and return to YOUR BASE (parasites only detach at base; a failed run loses both egg and parasite) → feed parasite to the monster (+20% meter each) → 5 parasites = 100% = one Monster Chest. Chest odds: 1.25x Egg Growth 43.5%, 1.25x Speed 30%, 2x Treadmill Speed 20%, Flyswatter 5%, Parasite/Monstrous Egg 1.5%. ~330 parasites per Parasite Egg on average. Buffs last 5 min; duplicate rolls RESET the timer rather than stack.

Frequent timed updates: Monster Update Aug 29 2026; Cherry Blossom biome added Aug 22 2026; Titan Temple added later; "Admin Abuse" events referenced; limited Shop eggs (Brainrot, Monster) rotate. Game description carries a like-gated drop: "Next Guaranteed Mythic Egg Drops at: 1,000 LIKES" (on Steal a Egg). Map layout itself has changed between updates since the July 2026 launch.
findings.source: stealanegg.net; eldorado.gg all-pets-index; stealanegg-roblox.wiki/eggs/; steal-anegg.wiki map guide; roblox.com/games/108053424714724

findings.detail: x2 Money: 399 Robux. x2 Growth Speed: 467 Robux. Speed shop sells +150K up to +1B Speed for Robux. Speed Multiplier tiers 1–10: from 3 Robux for 2x up to 649 Robux for 1024x (each tier doubles). Cash pack $24,000 for 49 Robux. Divine trail 399 Robux. A fully maxed Robux rebuild from a new account reaches ~3.4 billion speed in about 30 minutes — enough for Cherry Blossom (2.5B) but short of Titan Temple (7B). "The ceiling on this route is income, not speed."
findings.source: stealanegg.net; allthings.how money guide; allthings.how max-speed-fast; allthings.how trails

findings.detail: Biome perimeter walls affect guardian pathfinding. "Drop the egg inside a biome's perimeter wall and the kitsune or tiger cannot retrieve it after landing a hit, which lets you shuttle it toward spawn in slow, safe increments." Two players repeating the steal-and-drop loop inside a wall "can also break the area boss outright." This is the main way underleveled players extract high-tier eggs.
Official player-to-player trading is "not yet" implemented. Third-party marketplaces (Eldorado.gg) facilitate account/item transactions outside the game.

"Private servers unavailable; players can access 'fewest players' public servers via Roblox server browser." Sorting by fewest players is the standard way to reduce PvP interference — meaningful given the 7-player cap.

A large cluster of near-identical SEO domains (steal-an-egg-wiki.wiki, stealanegg-roblox.wiki, stealanegg.pro, steal-an-eggwiki.wiki, stealanegg.wiki, steal-an-egg.wiki, stealaneggguide.wiki, stealanegg.app, stealaegg.com) publish AI-generated content with FABRICATED numbers. Concrete tells: "Desert = Speed 50, Storm Peaks = Speed 100" (real Desert gate is 10,000; 'Storm Peaks' is not a real biome); "maintain egg temperature above 75% for a continuous 8-minute cycle"; "500 coins incubation cost"; "rebirth grants +5% passive income" (no rebirth exists in 107778070777162). RELIABLE TIER: roblox.com, rolimons.com, games.gg, eldorado.gg, allthings.how, bloxron.com, ldplayer.net, sportskeeda.com. Notably, steal-an-egg.github.io explicitly REFUSES to publish unverified numbers, which is a mark of quality but means it yields little concrete data.

openQuestions: Exact steal interaction duration: is there a hold-to-fill progress bar, and if so how many seconds, and does it scale with egg tier? Only one low-reliability source mentions a 'grab animation'; every reliable source describes a plain press-E proximity grab. Needs in-game verification or a video frame-count.

Exact carry speed penalty curve. The only figure found is 'Giant eggs cut sprint speed by 50%' from a single source. Unknown: the penalty for Small/Normal/Large, whether it is a flat multiplier or a subtraction, and whether it scales with the egg's kg weight value directly.
Starting number of pen equip slots and the maximum. No source publishes either. Only one data point exists on the cost curve (+1 EQUIP at $75M).
Whether jump height/jump ability is reduced while carrying (jumping is confirmed possible, but no source says whether the jump is nerfed).

Whether 'Steal An Egg' (107778070777162) actually has any base-raiding or a 'Security Defense Wall'. One unreliable source claims it; the official description and every reliable source describe theft only as mid-transit interception.

Concrete base-defense numbers for 'Steal a Egg' (108053424714724, Crazay Minds): lock/shield duration, door mechanics, steal cooldowns, troll gear cooldowns, and how many coin pads a plot has. Wikis reference these topics but publish no numbers.
Exact map distances or run-times from each biome nest back to the safe zone in studs or seconds — no source publishes any spatial measurement.
Bat swing cooldown, bat stun/ragdoll duration, and the inventory cap on bear traps.
Whether the ~4.5-minute figure and the ~5-minute figure are the same clock (day+night = 4.5 min total vs day = 5 min + 13s night). Sources disagree slightly; needs a stopwatch in-game.
Prehistoric biome speed gate: 17,000,000 or 18,000,000? Reliable sources split evenly.
Whether the night 30x growth multiplier requires the player to be actively in-game and moving, or applies to any placed egg server-side.

summary:
The "steal" genre is a PvP-flavored idle tycoon wearing a heist costume. Every entry (Steal a Brainrot, Steal a Fish, Steal a Labubu, Steal an Egg) runs the same skeleton: a ring of 6–10 base plots around one central attractor; a conveyor/nest that emits units on a timer; a slot grid where units become cash-per-second pedestals; a re-armable lock/forcefield (60s in Brainrot, 60s in Fish) as the only real defense; an 8-tier rarity ladder; a multiplicative mutation ladder (1.25x → 13x); a fuse machine; a collection Index; and a rebirth prestige (17 levels, ×0.5 → ×17 in Brainrot). Steal an Egg is the important divergence: it replaces "steal from other players' bases" with "steal from 10 PvE biome nests, each with one Guardian and one speed gate" (Forest 0 → Lake 900 → Desert 10K → Jungle 40K → Snow 170K → Volcano 700K → Abyss 2.5M → Prehistoric 18M → Cosmic 700M → Cherry Blossom 2.5B). Parkour For Brainrots goes further, deleting PvP entirely and gating everything on movement (four jumps, rooftops, a void). Those two are the proof that a single-player, obby-first "Steal an Egg" is a legitimate genre position, not a compromise.

Retention comes from loss aversion, not accumulation: this is one of the only mass-market loops where progress can be taken away, which is what makes the pedestal feel valuable. The tension beat is a fixed five-part arc — Bait (see the prize), Commit (grab, get slowed), Point of No Return (alarm/aggro), Chase (the run home, the game's only real skill test), Bank (slam it on the pedestal, number goes up). Everything else is scaffolding for repeating that arc every 30–90 seconds.

Converting to single-player means replacing four jobs PvP was doing (unpredictable threat, loss pressure, social comparison, free content generation) with Guardian archetypes + a heat system, egg fragility and a nest-raiding NPC, async ghosts/leaderboards, and rotating nest modifiers. Converting to first person makes the chase far more tense (you cannot see behind you) but breaks platforming legibility and the show-off loop — both fixable with a visible lower body, a glance-back, landing prediction, and a third-person Pen mode.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — ring of base plots around a central attractor
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot places 8 bases on the map arranged around one shared central conveyor area. This is the load-bearing layout of the genre: every plot has line-of-sight to the center, every player's loot is visible to everyone, and travel time between any two plots is short (roughly 5–15s of running). The ring does three jobs at once — it makes wealth legible (you can see who is rich), it makes the center a permanent contested chokepoint, and it keeps the walk-home distance short enough that a chase is a discrete beat rather than a commute.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — base slot grid and vertical expansion
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot base capacity: Floor 1 = 10 slots by default, Floor 2 = +8 slots unlocked at Rebirth 2, Floor 3 = +4 slots at Rebirth 10, for a maximum of 22 slots at Rebirth 13+. Slots are a hard scarcity that forces a constant 'is this new unit better than my worst unit' decision. Steal an Egg uses the same idea under a different name: the 'Pen', upgraded to increase how many pets are active at once.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — the conveyor / Red Carpet
findings.detail: Brainrots spawn from a cave entrance and walk along a studded path ('Red Carpet') toward a drop-off point. Any player can buy the unit off the belt. A second player can intercept a purchase by paying 150% of the original price, transferring ownership. Any unit that reaches the end of the path unbought disappears permanently. That last rule is the whole point: the conveyor is a use-it-or-lose-it timer that manufactures urgency every ~20 seconds without any scripted event.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — guaranteed rarity timers as appointment mechanics
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot guarantees a Legendary spawn every 5 minutes and a Mythic every 15 minutes; Secret and OG spawn at extremely rare random intervals and trigger server-wide announcements. This converts an idle game into a session with a heartbeat: players know exactly when the next 'be at the conveyor' moment is, which sets natural session length at ~15–30 minutes and gives them a reason to not alt-tab.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — lock/door defense with duration and re-arm
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot: laser gates at the base entrance; lock button grants 60 seconds of protection, +10s per rebirth level, +10s optional VIP; new players get 30s spawn protection regardless of rebirth. Steal a Fish: a Forcefield button gives a barrier that lasts exactly one minute and must be manually re-armed. Steal a Labubu: 'Lock Base' with a cooldown. The universal design is deliberately leaky — the lock is short, manual, and expiring, so the base is never actually safe and the player is never allowed to fully relax.

Every game in the genre resolves the prize into a static object on a pedestal that emits currency on a tick. Steal an Egg income spread: Chicken (Forest, Common) $1/s → Jerboa (Common ceiling) $6/s → Lava Iguana (Volcano, Legendary) $11K/s → Spider (Jungle, Mythic) $22K/s → King Mammoth (Snow, Cosmic) $400K/s → Whale Shark (Cosmic) $700K/s → Beluga Whale (Abyss, Cosmic) $850K/s → Bronto (Prehistoric, Cosmic) $1.5M/s → Cerberus (Volcano, Secret) $8M/s. Per-biome top pets run $1.8K/s (Forest) to $1B/s (Cosmic). The pedestal is the trophy case AND the economy AND the theft target — one object doing three jobs is why the genre is so legible.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — rarity ladder (8 tiers is the standard)
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot: Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Brainrot God, Secret, OG. Steal an Egg: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Cosmic, Secret. Eight tiers is the convergent answer — enough for a long ladder, few enough that a child can recite it. Note the top two tiers in both are named things rather than adjectives ('Brainrot God', 'Secret', 'Cosmic'), which reads as 'beyond the scale' and is what makes chase-tier announcements land.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — mutation ladder is multiplicative and cosmetically obvious
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot mutation multipliers: Gold ~1.25x (most common, permanent), Diamond ~1.5x (permanent), Lava 6x, Cursed 9x, Rainbow 10x (permanent), Divine 10x, Cyber 11x, Phantom 12x, Crystal ~13x. One mutation max per unit. Crucially each mutation also changes appearance (Phantom makes the unit transparent black-and-white), so value is readable at a glance from across the map — which is what makes a mutated unit worth stealing and worth defending.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — traits as a second, stacking multiplier layer
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot separates 'mutations' (one max, from the conveyor) from 'traits' (multiple can stack, never from the conveyor — only from admin events, player rituals, weather, or machines). Trait multipliers: Taco 3x, Asteroid/Galactic 4x, Crab Rave 5x, Paint ~5–6x, Nyan Cat/Firework 6x, Meowl ~7–8x, Strawberry ~8–9x. The design lesson is that having two independent multiplier axes lets you introduce new value ceilings for years without touching the rarity ladder.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — size and mutation as secondary roll on the same unit
findings.detail: Steal an Egg rolls both size and mutation on eggs/pets, and both affect income and hatch time. Sizes and mutations mean two identical-species pets can be worth wildly different amounts — this is what sustains grinding a biome you have already 'completed'.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — fuse machine (sink for duplicates)
findings.detail: Steal an Egg: combining three identical pets produces one higher-rarity version with greater income; per one source it improves the odds of a rarer result from that egg type rather than deterministically upgrading. Steal a Brainrot has an equivalent Fuse Machine with recipes and a rotating pool. Every game in the genre needs this because slot scarcity generates a constant stream of worthless duplicates, and a fuse machine converts that garbage into hope.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — Index / collection log with silhouettes
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot's Index shows silhouettes for uncollected units and grants permanent bonuses (base multipliers, cosmetics) at milestones. Steal an Egg's Pet Index gives free rewards on first-time discovery and, per one source, completing a location's index unlocks zone-specific bat skins with knockback bonuses. The Index is the genre's completionist retention layer and its main non-random progress track — the antidote to a pure-RNG ladder.

Steal a Brainrot has 17 rebirth levels with requirements escalating from $500K to $2.5 quadrillion, granting multiplicative income bonuses from ×0.5 to ×17, plus one extra base slot per level, longer base lock, new gear, and new floors. Steal a Labubu's rebirth resets stats/inventory/heist progress but preserves permanent unlocks, affinity levels, vault keys and blueprint fragments. The pattern: reset the number, keep the identity.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — the carry is deliberately slow and interruptible
findings.detail: Universal rule across all four games. Steal a Brainrot: thieves move slower while carrying a unit; if the owner stops the thief before delivery the unit is dropped and can be recovered. Steal a Labubu: hold E to pick up, and 'if someone hits you, you'll drop the plushie, and it returns to its owner.' Steal an Egg: large eggs create carry drag that reduces effective speed, and curved escape paths bleed momentum. Steal a Fish inverts it — a fish you BOUGHT walks slowly to your base on its own and can be stolen in transit. The carry is where 100% of the tension lives.

findings.topic: Genre skeleton — melee knockback tools rather than damage
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot defense is bats and slappers that knock thieves off your property, plus traps, sentries and gear that 'delay attackers rather than replacing Base Lock'. Steal an Egg has bat skins with knockback bonuses awarded from index completion. The genre never uses health/kill combat — it uses knockback that causes a DROP. That keeps the stakes on the object, not the avatar, which is why it stays age-appropriate and why every fight is legible.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg specifically — the PvE divergence that matters most for your game
findings.detail: Steal an Egg replaces 'raid other players' bases' with 'raid 10 PvE biome nests, each with exactly one Guardian, one egg pool, and one speed threshold.' Biome → Guardian → speed gate → top pet income: Forest/Chicken/0/$1.8K'/s; Lake/Swan/900/$220K'/s; Desert/Scorpion/10K/$280K'/s; Jungle/Tiger/40K/$3.5M'/s; Snow/Yeti/170K/$65M'/s; Volcano/Cerberus/700K/$100M'/s; Abyss Ocean/(unlisted)/2.5M/$130M'/s; Prehistoric/T-Rex/17–18M/$180M'/s; Cosmic/Cosmic Skeleton Boss/700M/$1B'/s; Cherry Blossom/(unlisted)/2.5B/$600M'/s. This is the single most important precedent for a single-player build: the genre already works with an NPC as the antagonist.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — no border gates, the speed check fires on PICKUP
findings.detail: 'You can walk into any biome at any speed since there are no border gates.' Speed requirements only activate upon egg collection. This is a genuinely good design choice worth copying: the player is allowed to walk into the scary zone, stand next to the T-Rex, and see the prize they cannot yet take. Aspiration is free; the wall only appears at the moment of commitment. It also means the world is fully explorable from minute one, which is exactly what an obby wants.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — failure state is ragdoll fling and the egg drops in the world
findings.detail: When a guardian catches you it 'triggers a ragdoll that flings you away from the biome, costing the entire run,' and 'the egg you were carrying drops on the ground' for other players to claim. Two things to note: (a) the ragdoll is comedic rather than punishing in tone, which keeps failure watchable, but (b) it costs the ENTIRE run with zero partial credit, which is the game's harshest anti-pattern.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — speed is trained by AFK treadmill, not by skill
findings.detail: The treadmill is unlocked with a $1,000 garden upgrade and provides AFK passive speed gain that scales per level. Trails are cosmetic items with direct speed multipliers, 10 of them from Common to Divine rarity. Social actions grant a one-off 10,000 free speed. This means the gate between biomes is AFK time, not player skill — which is exactly the design decision an obby-first game should reverse.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — the speed curve is brutally multiplicative
findings.detail: Consecutive gate ratios: 900 → 10K (11.1x) → 40K (4x) → 170K (4.25x) → 700K (4.1x) → 2.5M (3.6x) → 18M (7.2x) → 700M (39x) → 2.5B (3.6x). The Cosmic gate alone is a 39x jump. Because speed comes from an AFK treadmill, each of those multipliers is literal waiting. This is the main structural reason the game is described as repetitive, and the single clearest thing to avoid.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — hatching is deliberately session-locking
findings.detail: Eggs in your pen grow at 30x speed during the game's night cycle, which repeats every few minutes, making leaving the game 'the slow option'. Even at zero timer, 'the egg still does not open on its own — you have to return to the pen and press the hatch button.' Some rare eggs take hours. This is a raw retention screw: it converts idle timers into mandatory presence.

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — server-hopping is the optimal play, which is a design failure
findings.detail: Egg spawns are shared across active servers but the SIZE changes per server, so the optimal strategy is to server-hop to find a larger version before collecting; once picked up, the spawn disappears everywhere. Optimal play is therefore repeatedly leaving the game. Any single-player design must not create an equivalent (e.g. re-rolling a nest by rejoining).

findings.topic: Steal an Egg — mutation source is a gacha incubator with a punishing rate
findings.detail: Mutations are applied via the Sakura incubator at 97.5% Bloom / 2.5% Spirit. Pets can carry multiple mutations simultaneously (unlike Brainrot's one-max rule), compounding value.

findings.topic: Steal a Fish — the buy-then-escort inversion
findings.detail: In Steal a Fish, once you purchase a fish it walks slowly toward your base on its own and you must protect it in transit or lose it. This inverts the usual carry: instead of you being the vulnerable carrier, you become the escort of a vulnerable object with its own pathing. It creates a defend-a-moving-point beat that is distinct from both stealing and base defense, and is a strong idea to steal for a single-player game (escort the hatchling home past predators).

findings.topic: Steal a Labubu — the explicit two-playstyle framing
findings.detail: Steal a Labubu markets an explicit choice: 'play as a tycoon, carefully purchasing Labubus and fortifying your base, or play as a thief, infiltrating rival bases.' Players start with $100. Pickup is hold-E. This tycoon/thief dichotomy is how the genre gives risk-averse and risk-seeking players separate viable lanes in the same server.

findings.topic: 'Obby but you steal' subgenre — Parkour For Brainrots is the closest precedent to your game
findings.detail: Parkour For Brainrots: double/multi-jump through the sky and land on buildings, grab Brainrots and carry them back to your base to earn cash. Press spacebar to jump and 'you will have three more jumps left' — 4 total air-phases, with the multi-jumps resetting on landing. Higher and more distant buildings hold better loot. Don't fall into the void. Money buys upgrades to speed, carry capacity, and jump boosts, plus brainrot income upgrades. Critically: there is NO base defense and NO PvP stealing — the difficulty gate is entirely movement. This is direct evidence that the steal loop survives with movement as the sole antagonist.

findings.topic: 'Obby but you steal' subgenre — three upgrade axes worth copying verbatim
findings.detail: Parkour For Brainrots upgrades exactly three movement stats: speed, carry capacity, and jump boost. That triad maps perfectly onto an obby-steal loop — speed shortens the chase, jump opens vertical routes (new geography, not just bigger numbers), and carry capacity changes how many eggs you can bank per run (a risk/greed dial). Prefer these to a single 'speed' scalar because each one unlocks visibly different play rather than the same play, faster.

findings.topic: Retention — loss aversion is the actual engine, not accumulation
findings.detail: Multiple analyses converge on this: 'competition adds intensity and defense adds attachment. Players care about their assets because when something feels vulnerable, it feels valuable.' The steal genre is one of very few mass-market loops where accumulated progress can be taken away in real time. That vulnerability, not the number going up, is what makes the pedestal emotionally load-bearing. Any single-player conversion that removes ALL loss risk will feel hollow no matter how good the numbers are.

findings.topic: Retention — the canonical five-beat tension arc
findings.detail: Every successful run in this genre is the same five beats, and they should be authored deliberately: (1) BAIT — you see a prize you can identify and price from a distance, and it is visibly better than what you own. (2) COMMIT — you touch it, you get slower, and your options narrow. (3) POINT OF NO RETURN — an alarm fires; the world now knows. (4) CHASE — the return trip, where all skill expression lives. (5) BANK — placement on the pedestal, a satisfying thunk, and the income number visibly ticks up. Target 30–90 seconds for the full arc. If any beat is missing the run feels flat; if BANK lacks a loud audiovisual payoff the whole arc deflates.
findings.source: Synthesized from mechanics across all four games

findings.topic: Retention — variable reward plus a visible long-term goal from minute one
findings.detail: The named psychological mechanisms are: a variable reward system where 'players never know exactly when their next upgrade or rare drop will appear, but know it's coming'; a competence loop where visible progress feeds motivation; social validation from showing off bases; identity extension where 'possessions (even digital ones) become part of who we are'; and humour that 'masks the hook' so players don't feel like they're grinding. Roblox simulation retention guidance frames this as four layers with a core loop that fits inside 15–20 seconds and a long-term goal visible from minute one.

findings.topic: Retention — the first 10 seconds and first 5 minutes decide Day-1
findings.detail: Guidance for Roblox specifically: the most decisive moment is the first 10 seconds, where the game must communicate what is happening, what to do, and why it is exciting, with movement, sound or visual feedback and a small reward within reach; the stay-or-leave decision is made in the first five minutes. Players do not read tutorials — use visual cues (arrows, particles, glowing trails) and contextual tutorials triggered by normal play. Roblox's own docs recommend timed hints calibrated by playtest: in their reference project most players completed the action in 10 seconds, so the hint fired at 11 seconds.

findings.topic: Retention — server-wide announcements as free social proof and a raid siren
findings.detail: Secret/OG spawns in Steal a Brainrot trigger server announcements. This does double duty: it is a status broadcast for the winner (social validation) and a call-to-arms for everyone else (a target has appeared). In single-player you lose both halves and must replace them — see the async ghost/leaderboard findings.

findings.topic: Retention — scale of the outcome when this works
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot (SpyderSammy / DoBig Studios, 2025) is the only Roblox experience to have surpassed 25 million concurrent users, and the second to pass 20M CCU. The genre also now has legal weight: the Steal a Brainrot team filed a complaint against a Fortnite custom game 'Stealing Brainrots' alleging it copies 'user interface elements … in-game objects, artwork, level design, animations, design aesthetics.' Practical read: mechanics are not defensible in this space, but presentation is — and copying presentation too closely is now an actual legal risk.

findings.topic: Retention — genre conversion is strong but decay is fast
findings.detail: Industry read on the category: 'brainrot games run on viral memes and steal-and-defend mechanics, converting hard on first launch but rarely holding long term.' A steal game reliably wins the first session; the design work is entirely in weeks 2–8. Budget accordingly — front-load content variety and a non-RNG progress track (Index, obby course completion, movement mastery) rather than more multiplier tiers.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — losing to something you could not perceive
findings.detail: The worst feeling in the genre is being hit from off-screen and dropping the prize with no warning. In third person you at least have a 70-degree rear blind spot; in first person the blind spot is ~180 degrees. Rule to adopt: every loss must be preceded by at least 1.5 seconds of perceivable warning in a channel the player can actually sense from their current camera. If a guardian can catch you from behind, it must announce itself audibly and directionally before it can touch you.
findings.source: Synthesized; grounded in https://games.gg/roblox/guides/steal-an-egg-biomes-guide/ and stealth-AI guidance at https://www.toolify.ai/ai-news/inside-the-mind-of-a-stealth-game-guard-202391

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — losing to a stat wall rather than to skill
findings.detail: Steal an Egg's guardians are outrun by having a bigger Speed number, not by playing better. Once your number clears the threshold the biome is trivial; one point under, it is impossible. There is no skill band in between. For an obby-first game this is the cardinal sin: it deletes the reason the platforming exists. Fix: make speed a soft modifier that widens the margin for error, and make ROUTE and EXECUTION the actual determinant.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — all-or-nothing failure with no partial credit
findings.detail: Getting caught in Steal an Egg 'costs the entire run' via a ragdoll fling back to spawn. Two-minute investments vaporize instantly. Fix: tiered failure. Drop the egg where you stand (retrievable, guardian re-alerted); or crack it (hatches to a lower tier); or lose the mutation roll but keep the base egg. Reserve total loss for the highest-tier eggs where the player explicitly accepted that stake.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — the babysitting lock and mandatory presence
findings.detail: A 60-second manually re-armed lock punishes the player for looking away, going to the bathroom, or alt-tabbing — and it is a chore, not a decision. Steal an Egg compounds this with hatching that requires you to physically return and press a button even after the timer expires, plus a night cycle that makes being logged in 30x more efficient. These are all attendance taxes dressed as mechanics. In single-player, delete every one of them: hatch on completion, bank income offline, and never require a re-arm.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — AFK progression as the primary gate
findings.detail: The treadmill in Steal an Egg means the fastest route to the next biome is to leave your character running and do something else. Any system where 'not playing' is the optimal strategy actively teaches players to stop playing. Replace AFK-gated stats with gates that are earned by doing the thing the game is about — for an obby, clearing a route, hitting a time, or finding a shortcut.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — server-hopping / meta-play outside the game
findings.detail: Per-server egg size variance makes rejoining servers the optimal play in Steal an Egg. Similarly, Los Traders stock refreshing every ~30 minutes and Brainrot trading create out-of-game meta activity. Whenever the best play is a menu action rather than a gameplay action, the gameplay is being devalued. Single-player equivalent to avoid: letting players re-roll a nest by rejoining or by save-scumming.

Steal a Brainrot gates its rarest units behind a Secret Lucky Block costing 2,399 Robux (roughly $25–30 retail). Genre monetisation leans hard on gacha boxes as the shortcut around the entire progression curve. This is effective and also the most-cited source of resentment. A cleaner model for a skill-based single-player obby: sell cosmetics, convenience (extra pen slots, offline-income multiplier, checkpoint skips), and time — never the chase-tier eggs themselves.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — 'just waiting for good things to come'
