findings.detail: Direct player criticism of Steal a Brainrot: some features 'feel repetitive' and the game becomes 'just waiting for good things to come.' The failure mode is that once income exceeds what you can spend, the conveyor becomes a slot machine you stand next to. Fix for an obby-steal game: keep the player's hands on the controller. The prize should always be at the end of a traversal, never at the end of a timer.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — number fatigue at the top of the curve
findings.detail: Steal a Brainrot's rebirth 17 requires $2.5 quadrillion; Steal an Egg's Cherry Blossom gate is 2.5 billion speed. Once numbers exceed what a player can hold in their head, the rarity ladder stops communicating value and the only readable signal is the colour of the mutation glow. Practical countermeasure: cap the readable economy (use tiered currencies, or reset the scale at each prestige), and lean on the visual/audio identity of a tier rather than its integer.

findings.topic: Anti-pattern — clone fatigue and undifferentiated presentation
findings.detail: A developer posting a 'Steal a House' clone to the Roblox DevForum admitted the claimed twist was 'ima be honest with you idk … just said twist to get more attention.' Peer feedback centred on polish rather than mechanics: it felt 'unfinished' with bland aesthetics that alienate younger players, houses didn't persist between sessions, UI elements clipped off-screen, shop prices weren't visible, and tool purchasing had no constraints so it could be spammed. The named fix was differentiation in the thumbnail and description, not in the code. Read: in this genre, presentation and persistence bugs kill you faster than design flaws.

findings.topic: Single-player — the four jobs PvP is actually doing
findings.detail: Before replacing PvP, name what it provides: (1) UNPREDICTABLE THREAT during the carry — a non-deterministic antagonist you cannot fully learn; (2) LOSS PRESSURE — the possibility that banked progress evaporates, which is what makes ownership feel real; (3) SOCIAL COMPARISON — an audience for your base and a ladder to climb; (4) FREE CONTENT — other players generate infinite novel situations at zero authoring cost. A single-player build must fund all four separately. Most single-player conversions only replace (1) and then feel dead.

findings.topic: Single-player — Guardian roster should be built from the PvP player archetypes
findings.detail: Map each human griefing behaviour onto a distinct guardian AI so the roster has the same variety-of-threat that players provided. Concrete archetypes: THE CHASER (fast, straight-line, aggros on pickup, loses interest after N seconds or at a boundary — the baseline); THE CAMPER (slow, patrols the EXIT rather than the nest, so the danger is on the way out not in); THE INTERCEPTOR (spawns ahead of you on your projected route home, forcing an improvised re-route mid-carry); THE MAGPIE (does not hurt you — it snatches the egg out of your hands and flies a slow, chaseable arc, so failure becomes a second chase rather than an ending); THE SLEEPER (harmless until you make noise — sprinting, landing hard, or breaking a crate — teaching a stealth register); THE SWARM (individually trivial, collectively route-denying, used to close off the easy line). Each biome should introduce exactly one new archetype and then recombine.
findings.source: Design synthesis grounded in stealth-AI guidance at https://www.toolify.ai/ai-news/inside-the-mind-of-a-stealth-game-guard-202391 and guardian behaviour at https://games.gg/roblox/guides/steal-an-egg-biomes-guide/

findings.topic: Single-player — use graded awareness states, not binary detection
findings.detail: Stealth-design consensus: use a gradual 0–100% detection meter built from distance, light level and movement speed, with decay and forgiveness windows, multi-point visibility sampling (head/torso/feet) and raycast occlusion — not a binary seen/unseen flag. Guards run three states (patrolling / suspicious / alerted) colour-coded green/yellow/red, and the first step above idle should always produce an audio bark ('what was that noise?'). Hearing matters as much as sight: running, breaking objects, and hard landings should emit a noise radius. For an obby this is doubly valuable because it means SPRINTING is a real cost, which gives the movement system a tactical dimension beyond 'go fast'.

findings.topic: Single-player — a Heat system replaces the escalating server
findings.detail: In multiplayer, danger escalates naturally because more players arrive as the server gets richer. Single-player needs an explicit substitute. Proposal: a per-nest HEAT value, 0–5, that rises by +1 per successful steal from that nest and decays by 1 every few minutes. Heat drives guardian count, guardian speed, patrol density, and whether the nest spawns a rarer egg pool. This makes greed self-balancing: farm the same nest repeatedly and it becomes a genuine gauntlet, walk away and it cools. It also gives the player a dial they control, which is what makes escalation feel authored rather than punitive.

findings.topic: Single-player — invert the base defense into a raidable pen
findings.detail: You lose base defense entirely if nothing can attack you. Restore it PvE-style: a scheduled NPC raider (a Nest Mother reclaiming her egg, or a rival Collector) attacks your Pen on a visible timer — a countdown banner, an approaching silhouette on the horizon, an audio cue. The player must physically be at the Pen and defend, or lose one pedestal unit. Crucially, make it OPT-IN and SCHEDULED, never a surprise while offline: the raid announces itself 60 seconds ahead, only fires while the player is present, and offline periods simply skip it. That gives you the loss-aversion beat without any of the attendance tax.

findings.topic: Single-player — the DevForum consensus is that solo tycoons survive if the social layer survives
findings.detail: On whether a single-player-by-default Roblox tycoon is doomed: the concern is that 'a player is alone in his server [which] might push him to play something else,' and that players lost the motivation of visiting other bases to see aspirational goals. Proposed fixes: public gathering hubs, friend-base visitation, random base visits, global cross-server chat, and community groups. The counterargument from a responder: 'if the game is really good … I won't care if I was doing it by myself,' and simply KNOWING others could visit is enough motivation. Practical takeaway: keep the base visitable and shareable even if gameplay is solo.

findings.topic: Single-player — async ghosts and shared-world signals replace social comparison
findings.detail: Concrete replacements for the audience PvP provided: (1) GHOST RUNS — a translucent replay of your own best run or a friend's run on the same nest, racing beside you; costs almost nothing and directly restores the chase-a-rival feeling. (2) BLOODSTAINS / DROP MARKERS — Dark Souls style, show where other players failed on this obby section and what they were carrying, which makes the world feel populated without any netcode. (3) NEST LEADERBOARDS — fastest steal per nest, per week. (4) A VISITABLE PEN — let others walk your base read-only, which is the single feature the DevForum thread agreed matters most. (5) DAILY RIVAL — a named NPC collector whose score you must beat today, with a visible progress bar on the same nest.

findings.topic: Single-player — rotating modifiers replace players as the content generator
findings.detail: Other players were free, infinite content variety. The cheapest substitute is a roguelite modifier layer on top of static nests: rotate 2–3 daily modifiers per nest (Fog — halved audio range, doubled reward; Nesting Season — three eggs but the guardian never sleeps; Slippery — reduced friction; Blackout — the nest is dark and the egg glows; Migration — the nest has moved to a different route). This gets you a fresh-feeling run from the same geometry every day, which is exactly the authoring-cost problem PvP was solving.

findings.topic: Single-player — keep the object-loss stake, drop the player-loss stake
findings.detail: The genre's emotional core is that the OBJECT can be taken. In single-player, preserve that by making the egg itself the thing at risk (dropped, cracked, snatched by a Magpie, reclaimed by a guardian, taken in a scheduled Pen raid) while making the PLAYER's time cheap (fast respawn, checkpoint on entering each nest, no long walk back). Loss aversion survives; frustration does not.

findings.topic: First person — it is a tension multiplier, which suits this genre unusually well
findings.detail: First person makes the chase substantially scarier because you cannot see behind you — the same property that makes Lethal Company work, where the design 'leans on dread and audio cues rather than cheap jump-scares' and 'every element, from the crackle of the walkie-talkie to the deafening roar of a Forest Keeper, is perfectly tuned to maximize tension.' For a steal game the CHASE beat is the one you most want amplified, so the camera choice is aligned with the genre, not fighting it. Lethal Company also validates the carry mechanic directly: each item's weight incrementally slows the player, so 'that two-handed engine part worth 200 credits is tempting, but it will slow you down and make you an easy target' — this constant tension between greed and survival is the core of the design.

findings.topic: First person — you MUST render the lower body (this is non-negotiable for platforming)
findings.detail: Mirror's Edge's central solution: you can see yourself when looking downward, which is rare for first-person games. 'The visible body substitutes for proprioception, the sense of one's own body's position, which is particularly important for a platformer' and 'helps players judge exactly when to jump when running toward the edge of a roof.' DICE built hundreds of bespoke first-person animations and had to hand-massage every one because arms and feet aren't naturally visible enough when mocapping in first person. Concretely for your game: render legs/feet from a torso-down model, cull the head and upper arms from the local view, and allow camera pitch down to about -80 degrees so the player can look at their own feet on a ledge edge.

findings.topic: First person — head-bob must be conservative and toggleable
findings.detail: Head bob 'is a HUGE motion sickness trigger that should ideally always be able to be turned off in settings' and 'from a motion sickness perspective, no bob is always safer.' The classic sine-wave approach is criticised because its perfect regularity is unnatural; a recommended alternative is 'a slight roll to the camera on the stride instead of vertical bob, which produces a walking quality without the nausea-inducing up-down motion.' Concrete spec: vertical amplitude ≤1.5% of screen height, roll ±1.0–1.5 degrees on stride, frequency scaled to actual velocity, bob AMPLITUDE ZEROED while airborne (bobbing mid-jump is the single most disorienting mistake), plus a separate landing dip (see the landing finding). Ship a three-position setting: Full / Reduced / Off.

findings.topic: First person — FOV kick spec for sprinting and carrying
findings.detail: General guidance is to keep FOV in the 80–110 degree range with player control, and that framerate, FOV, reduced head bob and reduced motion blur are the main motion-sickness mitigations. Concrete spec for a first-person obby: base FOV 75–80; sprint adds +10 to +12 eased in over ~0.15s and eased out over ~0.25s (out slower than in, so deceleration feels like relief rather than a snap); carrying a heavy egg subtracts 4–6 and slightly narrows, which makes weight legible without a UI element; landing from height briefly subtracts 3 over 0.08s and returns over 0.2s. Expose an FOV slider (70–110) and a 'reduce camera effects' master toggle. In first person, FOV change is one of your only two speed cues — the other is the viewmodel — because there is no avatar to watch.

findings.topic: First person — the viewmodel is the genre's new trophy display
findings.detail: With no avatar visible, the hands and the carried egg become the entire visual identity of the player. Build: idle hand sway (small, out-of-phase with bob), a run cycle with visible pumping arms at the screen edges, a reach-out-and-grab animation on pickup that briefly fills the screen, and a strain animation for heavy eggs. The carried egg should sit low-centre or on the shoulder, occlude no more than ~15–20% of the lower screen, and visually communicate its rarity and mutation from the inside (glow, particles, cracks) so the player is looking at their prize the entire way home. This is the first-person replacement for the third-person 'everyone can see what you're carrying' status signal.

findings.topic: First person — the carried-egg vs look-down conflict, and how to resolve it
findings.detail: This is the real design tension of a first-person obby-steal: the carried object occupies exactly the screen space you need to see your feet for platforming. Three compatible mitigations: (1) TUCK POSE — when camera pitch drops below about -45 degrees, the egg animates into a hug/tuck against the chest and slides toward the screen edge, clearing the landing zone; (2) TRANSPARENCY RAMP — the egg fades to ~40% alpha when pitch is steeply down; (3) SHOULDER CARRY for large eggs so they sit above the sightline entirely, with the tradeoff that they block peripheral vision on one side (a real, readable cost that makes large eggs a genuine decision). Do not simply shrink the egg — its size is its value signal.

findings.topic: First person — you must add a glance-back
findings.detail: The chase beat depends on knowing how close the guardian is. In third person you simply see it; in first person you cannot. Add a hold-to-glance-back (Mirror's Edge Catalyst's approach to keeping the camera in the player's face while preserving orientation): holding the key swings the camera up to 180 degrees while the character KEEPS RUNNING in the original movement direction, with a slight FOV widen and a return ease of ~0.2s. This single input is the difference between the chase feeling tense and feeling arbitrary. Consider making it free early and never gating it behind an upgrade.

findings.topic: First person — guardian audio spec, since audio is now the primary threat channel
findings.detail: With ~180 degrees of blind spot, audio carries the entire rear-threat load. Required layers: (1) 3D spatialised, distance-attenuated footsteps whose TEMPO (not just volume) rises as the guardian closes, so proximity is readable even at low volume; (2) a distinct one-shot AGGRO bark at the point-of-no-return, mixed above everything, so the player always knows the exact frame the chase started; (3) a continuous proximity layer — breathing, growl, or a low rumble — that ducks the music, giving a smooth analog read on distance; (4) directional occlusion, so a guardian behind a wall sounds muffled and the player can tell it has line of sight; (5) a non-audio redundancy for deaf players and for muted mobile play — a directional threat arc on the screen edge, which doubles as the mobile-friendly solution since most Roblox mobile play is muted.
findings.source: Design synthesis grounded in https://www.toolify.ai/ai-news/inside-the-mind-of-a-stealth-game-guard-202391 and Lethal Company audio design per https://lethalcompanyreview.com/lethal-company-review-a-masterclass-in-chaotic-co-op-horror/

findings.topic: First person — landing prediction and edge peek
findings.detail: Two cheap additions that recover most of the platforming legibility lost with the camera: (1) LANDING MARKER — a subtle ground decal or projected shadow showing where the current arc will land, fading in only while airborne; even a soft blob shadow is enough, and it can be a difficulty/accessibility setting. (2) EDGE PEEK — when the player stands within ~1 stud of a ledge, ease the camera forward and down by a few degrees so the drop becomes visible without manual look-down. Both are invisible when not needed and remove the 'I couldn't see where I was going' complaint that kills first-person platformers.

findings.topic: First person — the show-off loop breaks and needs a third-person mode
findings.detail: Social validation and identity extension are named as core retention drivers, and both depend on seeing your own avatar and your own base. In locked first person you can do neither. Fix: a third-person orbit camera that is available ONLY inside your own Pen/base (and in a photo mode), so the tension camera and the trophy camera are separate tools. This also solves avatar-cosmetic monetisation, which is otherwise dead in a locked-FP game.

Coyote time is a brief grace window after leaving a platform during which a jump input still counts. Celeste uses 5 frames (~83ms at 60fps); Super Meat Boy uses a similar duration. The rationale given is perceptual: the human eye processes visual information roughly 13ms behind reality, so by the time the player sees the character leave the edge it has already been airborne for several frames. RECOMMENDED FOR FIRST-PERSON: 0.12s baseline (longer than Celeste's 83ms, because first person removes the visual cue of seeing your own feet leave the ledge), extended to 0.16–0.18s while carrying an egg, since the carry already occludes the feet.

Jump buffering means a jump pressed shortly before landing fires on the exact frame of landing. Celeste counts down roughly 4 frames (~67ms); general guidance puts the useful range at 0.1–0.2 seconds of pre-queued input. RECOMMENDED: 0.15s. Coyote time and input buffering are described as 'the two most impactful forgiveness mechanics in platformer design,' and games without them 'feel like they cheat the player.' Both are cheap to implement in Roblox — the DevForum has a ready community resource.

findings.topic: Parkour feel — variable jump height and asymmetric gravity
findings.detail: Standard spec: releasing the jump button during ascent cuts vertical velocity (or applies an ascent-cut gravity multiplier), giving variable jump height. Falling uses a higher gravity multiplier than rising — Celeste uses about 2.5x, Super Mario about 2x. Celeste additionally applies HALF gravity at the top of the jump while the button is held, producing an apex float. RECOMMENDED: rise gravity 1.0x, apex float 0.5x while |vertical velocity| < ~3 studs/s, fall 2.2x, ascent-cut 2.5x on early release. The apex float is disproportionately valuable in first person because it gives the player extra time to look down and locate the landing.

findings.topic: Parkour feel — air control and the momentum-readability tradeoff
findings.detail: Quality-of-life patterns cited: lower gravity near the top of the jump giving more airtime, and faster horizontal movement at the apex. RECOMMENDED SPEC for first-person: air acceleration at 0.6–0.8 of ground acceleration (enough to correct, not enough to make jumps trivial), horizontal air speed capped at ground speed +10%, and — important and often missed — a TURN RATE CAP in air of roughly 360 degrees/second so an instant 180 is impossible. Uncapped air turning is what makes first-person movement feel weightless and floaty; capping it is what makes a jump feel committed.

findings.topic: Parkour feel — ledge grab and corner correction
findings.detail: Named pattern: 'players just missing a jump being able to climb up a corner if they hold into the edge.' RECOMMENDED SPEC: on a failed jump, run a forward+down capsule cast for 0.2s after apex; if a ledge is found within roughly 2 studs of hand height and the player is holding forward, snap into a hang and auto-mantle over 0.3–0.35s with the camera rising through the motion. Separately, CORNER CORRECTION: if the head clips a corner by ≤1 stud on the way up, nudge the player horizontally around it rather than killing the jump — first person makes headroom impossible to judge, so this matters more here than in 2D. Also add auto-step-up for lips ≤2 studs so small geometry never stops a run.

findings.topic: Parkour feel — camera tilt and landing dip spec
findings.detail: Camera roll is the first-person substitute for seeing your avatar lean. RECOMMENDED: ±1.5–2 degrees roll on strafe, eased over ~0.15s; 4–6 degrees during a wall-run, with the roll direction indicating which side the wall is on; 2–3 degrees roll into the direction of a hard turn at speed. LANDING DIP: pitch down 3–6 degrees over ~0.1s scaled by fall distance, recovering over ~0.25s, paired with a knee-bend in the visible legs and a landing thud. The landing dip is doing real work in first person — it is the only confirmation the player gets that they successfully landed, since they cannot see their body contact the ground.
findings.source: Design synthesis grounded in https://itch.io/post/303719 and Mirror's Edge camera practice per https://www.gameanim.com/2010/11/05/creating-first-person-movement-for-mirrors-edge/

findings.topic: Parkour feel — responsiveness is also a motion-sickness issue
findings.detail: Guidance: 'ensure movement is responsive and input-synchronized — animation lag between input and visual response is a primary motion sickness cause,' and avoid screen-space effects that persist for more than a second. This means every camera effect above (FOV kick, roll, landing dip) must be short and must never delay the actual movement response. Never gate movement behind an animation; drive the animation from the movement state.

findings.topic: Roblox implementation — baseline movement numbers and what to change
findings.detail: Roblox defaults: WalkSpeed 16, JumpPower 50, Workspace.Gravity 196.2. With JumpPower 50 you clear roughly an 11-stud block. Practical note for first person: WalkSpeed 16 reads as noticeably SLOWER in first person than in third, because there is no avatar animation selling the speed — budget a base of roughly 20–24 with a sprint to 30–34, and lean on FOV kick, viewmodel arm pumping and speed lines to sell it. Consider raising gravity above 196.2 with a correspondingly higher JumpPower for a snappier, less floaty arc; floatiness is much more objectionable in first person.

Enum.CameraMode.LockFirstPerson (set via Players.LocalPlayer.CameraMode) gives locked first person cheaply, but developers report it does not transition instantly when switched at runtime and gives no control over bob or body. For real control you need a custom camera driven in RunService.RenderStepped bound at Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, writing Camera.CFrame directly, with the viewmodel welded to the camera. Humanoid.CameraOffset is the cheap route to head-bob but is limited. A community 'First Person Mode' resource exists covering locked first person, custom camera placement, neck movement and body rotation. Also set Humanoid.AutoRotate = false and rotate the character manually so camera pitch and body yaw are decoupled — this is what lets you look down at your feet without the body tipping.

findings.topic: Recommendation — the core structural thesis for your game
findings.detail: Take Steal an Egg's PvE nest structure (proven), Parkour For Brainrots' movement-as-the-only-gate (proven, and the closest existing relative), and Steal a Brainrot's presentation/economy scaffolding (rarity ladder, mutation ladder, index, pedestal income, prestige). Then make the ONE substitution the genre has never made: replace the speed STAT gate with a movement SKILL gate. The nest is not locked behind 700,000 treadmill points; it is locked behind a route you can actually run. That is a genuine differentiator in a saturated genre, it is exactly what first person amplifies, and it means the obby is load-bearing rather than decorative.

Given that the stay-or-leave decision happens in the first 10 seconds and first 5 minutes: 0–5s, player spawns in first person looking directly at a glowing egg on a low nest 15 studs away with one visible sleeping chicken guardian — no text. 5–15s, they grab it (hands reach out, egg fills the lower screen, a bark fires, the chicken wakes). 15–30s, a short 4-jump obby back to the Pen with a glowing trail (Roblox's recommended visual-cue onboarding). 30–40s, they slam it on a pedestal, it hatches immediately with a big audio payoff, and the income counter starts ticking visibly. 40–90s, a second nest is visible slightly higher up with an obviously better egg. The entire genre pitch — steal, run, bank, want more — has been delivered without a single line of tutorial text.

findings.topic: Recommendation — carry weight as the central risk dial
findings.detail: Adopt the Lethal Company weight model rather than a binary carrying flag: bigger/rarer eggs apply a continuous penalty to WalkSpeed, jump height, air control and turn rate, so the player physically feels the value of what they hold and every route decision is re-evaluated. Combined with carry capacity as an upgrade (per Parkour For Brainrots), this gives you the genre's greed-vs-survival tension with zero PvP. Make the penalty visible in the viewmodel (strain, lower carry position, heavier breathing) rather than in a UI number.

findings.topic: Recommendation — what to deliberately NOT copy from the genre
findings.detail: Cut list, in priority order: (1) the manually re-armed 60-second base lock — replace with the scheduled opt-in PvE raid; (2) the AFK treadmill — replace with skill/route-based gates; (3) manual hatch-button-after-timer and the 30x night cycle — hatch automatically, bank offline income; (4) per-server RNG that rewards rejoining; (5) total run loss with no partial credit — use drop/crack tiers; (6) quadrillion-scale numbers — use a tiered currency or reset the scale each prestige; (7) chase-tier gacha boxes at 2,399 Robux — monetise cosmetics, pen slots, offline multipliers and checkpoint conveniences instead.

findings.topic: Recommendation — accessibility and settings checklist (ship these, they are cheap)
findings.detail: Camera effects: Full / Reduced / Off for head-bob, landing dip, camera roll, and FOV kick independently. FOV slider 70–110. Landing-marker toggle. Directional threat indicator toggle (also serves muted mobile players, who are the majority on Roblox). Sprint toggle vs hold. Look sensitivity separate for X and Y. Motion-sickness guidance is explicit that head-bob should always be disableable and that framerate, FOV and reduced bob are the primary mitigations — and in a locked-first-person Roblox game aimed at a young audience, shipping without these will cost you players who physically cannot play.

openQuestions: Is the game single-player-only, or single-player-by-default with visitable bases? The DevForum consensus is that solo tycoons survive if the SOCIAL layer survives (visitable pens, leaderboards, ghosts) — the answer changes how much async infrastructure needs building.

Target platform mix: locked first person plus precision platforming is significantly harder on mobile touch controls, and Roblox mobile is a large share of the audience. Does the design assume PC/console primary, or does it need a mobile-viable control scheme (auto-run, larger coyote/buffer windows, assisted landing)?

Is the obby course fixed and authored, or procedurally assembled per run? Authored gives better feel and better speedrun leaderboards; procedural solves the single-player content-generation problem that PvP used to solve for free. A hybrid (authored nest interiors, rotating daily modifiers) is probably right but needs a decision early.
How harsh should failure be? Recommended tiered failure (drop / crack / lose mutation) requires deciding whether eggs are individually tracked objects with state, which affects the whole data model.

Does the player have any combat/tool verb at all (a bat, a net, a distraction item), or is the entire verb set movement? A pure-movement verb set is cleaner and more distinctive, but removes the option to ever push back on a guardian.

Monetisation model: cosmetics-and-convenience is recommended over the genre-standard gacha lucky blocks, but the genre's revenue is demonstrably driven by those boxes. Is there an appetite to accept lower ARPU for a cleaner, more defensible design?

How large is the art/animation budget? The visible-lower-body plus bespoke first-person viewmodel requirement (Mirror's Edge needed hundreds of hand-tuned FP animations) is the single largest cost item implied by the first-person decision.

summary:
Steal An Egg (Roblox place 107778070777162, universe 10563114921, by "and Collect Rare Pets", launched 25 Jul 2026; ~1.3B visits, ~1.5M CCU as of 3 Sep 2026) runs a single-currency ($ "Money"/Coins) tycoon loop with ONE hard gate: Speed.

LOOP: steal egg from a biome nest guarded by a boss -> carry it home (heavy eggs slash your movement) -> hatch in pen -> pet pays passive $/s forever -> spend $ on Treadmill tier + Trail tier -> train Speed -> unlock next biome. Start = 10 Speed, $0 cash. Income is fully passive/auto-credited (no click-to-claim) and accrues offline.

SPEED IS THE GATE because it is the only unlock key AND the only escape mechanic. 11 biomes gate at 0 / 900 / 10K / 40K / 170K / 700K / 2.5M / 17-18M / 700M / 2.5B / 7B — a 7.8-million-fold climb from Lake to Titan Temple. Cash cannot buy Speed directly (F2P); it buys Speed *rate* multipliers: Treadmill 10 tiers 2x->2000x costing Free/$15K/$250K/$5M/$120M/$3B/$75B/$2T/$50T/$1Q, and Trail 10 tiers 1.5x->14x costing $100/$5K/$75K/$1.5M/$30M/$750M/$20B/$500B/$12.5T/$300T. Both curves cost ~x20-25 per tier while delivering only ~x2-2.5 benefit — a deliberate 10:1 squeeze that forces you back to better biomes for income. Max stacked F2P speed rate = 2,000 x 14 = 28,000x. The rest is treadmill AFK time.

INCOME SPAN: $1/s (Chicken) -> $3B/s (Nightflame) = 3-billion-fold across 10 rarity tiers. Best-in-biome ladder: Forest $1.8K/s -> Lake $220K/s -> Desert $280K/s -> Jungle $3.5M/s -> Snow $65M/s -> Volcano $100M/s -> Abyss $130M/s -> Prehistoric $180M/s -> Cosmic $1B/s -> Cherry Blossom $1.8B/s -> Titan Temple $3B/s. Multiplied by Color mutation (x1.2-x3.5) and Size (x1 Normal, x3 Giant, x5 Huge; empirically up to ~x100 by kg).

REBIRTH (Aug 2026): 6 tiers, each +5% permanent passive income (max +30%); resets pets, income, pen upgrades and Speed; keeps permanent bonuses. Speed 150 doubles mutation chance. Community times: ~1/2/4/6/10/14h.

CODES: none exist — there is no redeem box. Reward economy runs on a free-gift panel (+10,000 Speed for like+favorite+group join) and events (Monster Chest table: 43.5% 1.25x egg growth, 30% 1.25x speed, 20% 2x treadmill, 5% flyswatter, 1.5% Monstrous Egg).

MONETIZATION: 2 gamepasses (X2 Money 399 R$, X2 Growth Speed 467 R$) plus dev products: treadmill tiers 39-799 R$, trails 8-399 R$, 10 Speed Multiplier tiers 2x@3R$ doubling to 1024x@649R$, Speed packs +150K@79R$ to +1B@2999R$, Instant Hatch ~9R$, Grow All ~160R$.

No luck/jump/stamina upgrade lines are documented — the only stat axes are Speed rate, Speed multiplier, pen equip slots (start 7, +1 EQUIP $1M early -> $75M later, 14+ observed), egg growth speed, and mutation rolls.

Whether offline pay is throttled vs online is unresolved. The one quoted example '$16M/Day offline' equals ~$185/s, which would be a very small pen; no source states a throttle percentage.

findings.topic: TREADMILL — cost curve shape (the key design number)
findings.detail: Cost step ratios tier-to-tier: 16.7x, 20x, 24x, 25x, 25x, 26.7x, 25x, 20x (after the first $15K step). Multiplier step ratios: 2.5x, 2.4x, 2.5x, 2.67x, 1.25x, 2x, 2.5x, 2x, 2x. So cost grows ~10x faster than benefit each tier. Cost per +1x of multiplier: $5,000 at Sci-Fi -> ~$1,000,000,000,000 at Angelic — a ~200-million-fold efficiency decay across the ladder.

Speed accrues per second while standing/running on the treadmill (AFK-able). Tier multiplier scales the per-second rate; Trail multiplies on top of that rate. One guide states an 8-hour AFK session at a high treadmill tier clears the Desert and Jungle thresholds (10K–40K).

findings.detail: Added August 2026. Each rebirth grants a PERMANENT +5% passive income bonus that stacks and never resets. Reaching Speed 150 doubles egg mutation chance (one source: from ~2% to ~4% base; this conflicts with the 11% roll-weight total from Fandom). RESETS: pet collection and all pet income, pen/base upgrades, and Speed from treadmill training (so biome access is lost). PERSISTS: the stacked +5% income bonuses and improved mutation odds.

Community-reported 6-tier ladder: R1 +5% total, ~1 hour ('cheap, do it fast'); R2 +10%, ~2 hours; R3 +15%, ~4 hours; R4 +20%, ~6 hours (aligns with first Mythic eggs); R5 +25%, ~10 hours ('the heavy grind begins'); R6 +30%, ~14 hours (current maximum / endgame objective). Rebirth 6 is the cap as of this data.

Multiple wikis state explicitly that the developer has published NO official rebirth spec, and community sources disagree on what resets. Also note: a +5%-per-rebirth income bonus capped at +30% is trivially small next to a 3,000,000,000x income span — so rebirth in this game is a cosmetic-scale prestige, NOT a real economy multiplier. Do not mirror it as a core loop driver.

Eggs respawn / nests reset every 5 minutes (one source says ~4.5 min, tied to the in-game night). Day lasts ~5 minutes, night ~10 seconds. findings.detail: There are ZERO codes. Because there are no codes, the 'free reward' scale is set by: (1) the Free Gift panel — like the game + favourite the game + join the community group = 10,000 Speed one-time (that is 11.1x the Lake gate of 900, and 25% of the Jungle gate — a deliberately generous onboarding shove that skips the first two biomes); (2) event chests; (3) event eggs. Unlock: hatch a Crane from a Cherry Blossom Egg -> bring it to the ancient Sakura tree -> restore the tree. Then place a pet inside and feed Sakura Crystals to charge it. LOW charge = chance at Bloom (x1.25); FULL charge = GUARANTEED Spirit Bloom (x2.5). Charge DECAYS if idle, so crystals must be fed in a steady stream rather than banked. The Great Bloom event (spawns giant crystal trees) fires every 30 minutes.

Players can steal eggs from other players' bases (not just from nests). Defensive item: Bear Traps — infinite supply but MAX 3 placed at once, only interactable while holding an egg, immobilise a victim for 7 seconds, cannot be placed in the safe zone, and are recovered when triggered or picked up.

The only quantified anchors are: the rebirth ladder times (R1 ~1h, R2 ~2h, R3 ~4h, R4 ~6h, R5 ~10h, R6 ~14h cumulative-ish, and R4 is stated to align with 'first Mythic eggs'); an 8-hour AFK session at a high treadmill tier clears Desert (10K) and Jungle (40K); and the community rule of thumb of 'one Rebirth per two to three full biome chains'. Mapping rebirth hours onto biomes suggests roughly: Forest->Lake minutes; Lake->Desert ~1h; Desert->Jungle ~1-2h; Jungle->Snow ~2-4h; Snow->Volcano ~4-6h; Volcano->Abyss ~6-10h; Abyss->Prehistoric ~10-14h; Prehistoric->Cosmic is the 39x wall and is where most F2P players stall for days.

findings.topic: Why Speed is the main gate — the design argument
findings.detail: Four reinforcing reasons: (1) Speed is the ONLY biome unlock key — there is no level, no quest, no key item. (2) Speed is also the ESCAPE mechanic against the guardian, so it gates the same content twice (enter vs. get out alive). (3) Egg weight subtracts from effective speed (Giant eggs ~-50% sprint), so the richest eggs in a biome require far more than the listed threshold — a soft third gate. (4) Cash cannot buy Speed directly, only speed-RATE multipliers whose cost curve (~x25/tier) massively outruns their benefit curve (~x2.2/tier), so cash always converts to Speed at a worsening exchange rate, guaranteeing that time-on-treadmill remains the binding constraint at every stage.
findings.source: INFERRED — synthesis across zone table, treadmill/trail cost data, and carry-weight sources

summary:
"Steal An Egg" (Roblox, by "and Collect Rare Pets", created July 2026, Simulation/Tycoon, 7-player servers, 1.3B+ visits) is a steal-and-extract loop, NOT a stealth game. Eleven biomes each hold one Guardian — a giant voxel version of that biome's signature animal — that SLEEPS beside its nest. There is no sight cone, no noise system, no patrol-and-detect phase and no post-grab countdown timer. Aggro is a single scripted event: the instant you pick up an egg a "RUN!!" banner appears and that Guardian wakes and chases. The entire encounter resolves as one pure stat race — Guardian's fixed per-biome speed vs. your Speed stat (a persistent number trained on Treadmills, multiplied by Trails), minus the carry-drag of the egg's size. Cross your safe-zone boundary and the Guardian hard-disengages instantly and returns to its nest; drop the egg mid-chase and it turns around, retrieves the egg, and walks it back.

Guardians and speed gates: Forest/Chicken (0), Lake/Swan (900), Desert/Scorpion (10K), Jungle/Tiger (~40K), Snow/Yeti (~170K), Volcano/Hellhound-Cerberus (~700K), Abyss Ocean/Moby (~2.5M), Prehistoric/T-Rex (17–18M), Cosmic/Dragon (700M), Cherry Blossom/Nine-Tailed Fox-Kitsune (2.5B, practical 3.5B), Titan Temple/Gorilla King (7B). That is the ONLY published scaling axis — no guardian speeds, HP, or aggro radii exist anywhere, because none are exposed in-game.

On catch: you are ragdolled and flung back to spawn, the egg drops and returns to the nest. No published stun timer, no money loss — the fling IS the penalty. Counterplay is thin and deliberate: Speed, Bear Traps (max 3, infinite supply, only equippable while holding an egg, blocked inside safe zones, 5–7s lock), per-biome Bats unlocked via Pet Index completion, and the drop-the-egg reset trick. There are no smoke bombs, invisibility, stamina bars, or stun weapons vs. guardians.

PvP is interception-only: anyone can bat you into a ragdrop or trap you anywhere on the map, but once an egg reaches your pen it is permanently safe — no base raiding, no cooldowns, no revenge system. Server-wide rare-egg spawn announcements every 5-minute reset cycle are the real tension engine, converting the whole server into a race.

findings.detail: "Steal An Egg" on Roblox, game ID 107778070777162, by developer "and Collect Rare Pets". Created July 2026. Genre Simulation / Subgenre Tycoon. Server Size: 7 players. Voice Chat: Not Supported. Camera: Not Supported. Maturity: Minimal. As read on 2026-09-03: 1,465,712 active players, 2,007,921 favorites, 1.3B+ visits, last updated 9/3/2026. Official Roblox description lists exactly seven bullets: steal eggs from pets; hatch eggs to collect rare pets; earn money from your pets; upgrade your treadmill AND base; train on the treadmill to increase speed; steal eggs from OTHER PLAYERS; discover rarer eggs, pets, sizes and mutations. findings.topic: Guardian roster — complete list per biome
findings.detail: 11 biomes, one Guardian each. 1 Forest — Chicken (no speed req). 2 Lake — Swan (900). 3 Desert — Scorpion (10,000). 4 Jungle — Tiger (~40,000). 5 Snow — Yeti (~170,000). 6 Volcano — Hellhound (~700,000). 7 Abyss Ocean — Moby (~2,500,000). 8 Prehistoric — T-Rex (~17,000,000–18,000,000). 9 Cosmic — Dragon (700,000,000). 10 Cherry Blossom — Nine-Tailed Fox (2,500,000,000). 11 Titan Temple — Gorilla King (7,000,000,000). Progression order is strictly linear: Forest → Lake → Desert → Jungle → Snow → Volcano → Abyss Ocean → Prehistoric → Cosmic → Cherry Blossom → Titan Temple.
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Zones and /wiki/Area (read directly); corroborated by games.gg, eldorado.gg, allthings.how, stealanegg.pro

findings.detail: Several guardians have contested names across sources. VOLCANO: 'Hellhound' (Fandom Zones, eldorado, stealanegg.pro) vs 'Cerberus' (games.gg) — the Volcano biome's SECRET pet is the Cerberus Egg, so both likely refer to the same three-headed-dog-themed entity. COSMIC: 'Dragon' (Fandom, eldorado) vs 'Cosmic Skeleton Boss' (games.gg) — the Fandom Cosmic Skeleton Boss page states 'Coincidentally, the boss of the Cosmic biome is also the Cosmic Skeleton Boss'. CHERRY BLOSSOM: 'Nine-Tailed Fox' (Fandom Cherry Blossom page, eldorado), 'Oni Tiger' (Fandom Zones table), 'Kitsune' (allthings.how glitch guide), 'Mother Crane' (bloxron). TITAN TEMPLE: 'Gorilla King' (Fandom) vs 'King Gorilla' (sportskeeda/techwiser). The Fandom Zones page itself carries a disclaimer that guardian names 'may change after game updates' and that 'Cherry Blossom's Guardian is listed as Unknown until confirmed by an official source.'

Kitsune and Nine-Tailed Fox are the same creature (kitsune literally means a nine-tailed fox spirit). Kitsune is the DIVINE-rarity top pet of the Cherry Blossom egg pool. Every other biome's guardian is drawn from that biome's own pet list, so the Cherry Blossom guardian is almost certainly the Kitsune / Nine-Tailed Fox. The 'Oni Tiger' entry in the Fandom Zones table is likely a stale edit (Oni Tiger is the ETERNAL pet of that biome, one tier below Kitsune), and 'Mother Crane' from bloxron is likely fabricated SEO content.
findings.source: cross-reference of stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Eggs pet pools against guardian names

findings.topic: Guardians are giant versions of biome pets
findings.detail: The Fandom Chicken page states the Chicken 'serves as both an entry-level pet for new players and the starter guardian of the Forest biome'. Every guardian maps onto a pet in its own biome's egg pool: Swan (Lake, EPIC), Scorpion (Desert, MYTHIC), Tiger (Jungle, MYTHIC), Yeti (Snow, SECRET), Cerberus (Volcano, SECRET), T-Rex (Prehistoric, SECRET), Cosmic Dragon / Cosmic Skeleton Boss (Cosmic, SECRET), Kitsune (Cherry Blossom, DIVINE), Gorilla King (Titan Temple, ETERNAL). The guardian is a scaled-up parent standing over the nest of its own species' eggs. Note the rarity tier of the guardian's pet form CLIMBS with biome tier (Common → Epic → Mythic → Secret → Eternal → Divine), which is a soft form of guardian scaling.

Directly observed from wiki art (ForestGuardian.png). A blocky voxel/Lego-style chicken in white-to-pale-lavender, built from visible cube studs. Red segmented comb on top of head, orange/gold square beak, small black square eyes. Squat, wide, ground-hugging body. A large glossy cyan-blue cartoon 'Z' with black outline floats above it, indicating sleep.

Directly observed. Voxel swan in white with pale blue/periwinkle shading, curved S-neck built from stacked cubes, small orange beak block, black dot eye, folded wing plates along the flank. Two stacked cyan 'Z' glyphs float to its upper left.

Directly observed. Tan/sand-gold voxel scorpion, symmetrical and front-facing. Segmented tail raised vertically behind the body ending in a bulbous stinger. Two large blocky pincers held forward and low. Flat carapace with four black cross/plus-shaped eyes on the head plate. Three cyan 'Z' glyphs of descending size float in front of the raised tail.

Directly observed. Bright orange voxel tiger with thick black vertical stripes across the back and flank, white muzzle, white chest bib, white paws with black toe blocks, pink tongue lolling out, one closed sleepy eye with a red inner detail, white square teeth. Shown lying down / crouched low in profile. A cyan 'Z' floats at the lower left near the head.

Directly observed. Large hunched white/off-white blocky ape with long arms reaching the ground, dark navy-black face recessed under a heavy brow, glowing cyan ice-crystal spikes protruding from the shoulder/back, black clawed feet. Bipedal but stooped forward. A cyan 'Z' floats at the right side of its head.

Directly observed. A long, low, quadrupedal beast in black obsidian/charcoal voxel plating with a dark cracked hide, shown in profile. Bright orange-and-yellow lava flames erupt in a jagged crest along the entire spine, on the head, and at the tail tip; red-hot glowing cracks run through the body. Reads more as a lava dragon/drake silhouette than a three-headed dog, which is worth noting against the 'Hellhound/Cerberus' naming.

Only six guardian renders exist on the wiki (Forest, Lake, Desert, Jungle, Snow, Volcano). Abyss Ocean, Prehistoric, Cosmic, Cherry Blossom and Titan Temple guardian image files are referenced by the zone pages but return 'missing' from the MediaWiki API — the zone pages render them as broken file links. No visual reference is publicly documented for the top five guardians. By biome theme they would be: a giant whale ('Moby'), a T-Rex, a cosmic dragon or star-skeleton, a nine-tailed fox, and a crowned gorilla.
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com api.php imageinfo query (run directly) — AbyssOceanGuardian.png, PrehistoricGuardian.png, CosmicGuardian.png all return "missing"

findings.topic: AI — idle state is SLEEPING, not patrolling
findings.detail: The Fandom wiki states plainly: 'The eggs are protected by dangerous monsters that SLEEP next to their nests. Players must approach, steal the eggs, and run to avoid being caught by the monsters.' This is confirmed independently by the art: ALL SIX guardian renders show a floating cyan 'Z' sleep glyph. The guardian is a dormant obstacle parked on the nest, not a moving patrol.
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Eggs and /wiki/Eggs_%26_pet (read directly); six guardian PNGs viewed

findings.topic: AI — the 'patrol loop' claim is contradicted
findings.detail: stealanegg.pro claims 'most guardians patrol a small loop around the nest' and that you should 'time your approach during the patrol's far swing'; games.gg says to 'look at the Guardian's patrol pattern'. This contradicts the Fandom wiki's sleep description and the sleep-glyph artwork. These sites are SEO/AI-generated aggregators with no first-party sourcing. Treat 'patrol' as unverified, most likely fabricated to pad the guide.

findings.topic: AI — aggro trigger is the egg pickup, not proximity
findings.detail: 'The moment you grab it, the RUN!! warning appears and that specific boss starts chasing you.' Aggro is a scripted event bound to the theft action, not to a proximity/vision check. stealanegg.pro concurs: 'When you grab an egg, the guardian immediately aggros to you and chases at its base speed.' You can therefore walk right up to a sleeping guardian safely; there is no approach phase to fail.

findings.topic: AI — 'detection radius' claims have no numbers and are likely fabricated
findings.detail: stealanegg.pro asserts a per-guardian detection radius that 'scales by guardian size — smaller creatures like chickens have tight radii; larger guardians like Dragons have wide ones', and calls the T-Rex radius 'huge' and the Scorpion's 'wider'. NO source anywhere gives a single numeric radius, in studs or otherwise. Given the aggro-on-pickup mechanic and the sleeping idle state, a proximity detection radius probably does not exist in the shipped game.
findings.source: stealanegg.pro/guide/how-to-steal-eggs (uncorroborated); absence across Fandom, games.gg, eldorado, allthings.how

findings.detail: The guardian pursues in direct straight-line pursuit at a fixed per-biome speed. It chases ACROSS THE ENTIRE MAP, including all the way back toward the lobby/spawn area — there is no leash distance or chase-timeout. The outcome is decided purely by whether your effective movement speed exceeds the guardian's for the duration of the return trip. Chase duration is therefore distance-based, a function of how far the nest is from your safe zone, not a timer.
findings.source: allthings.how boss-glitches article; games.gg beginner guide; eldorado.gg biomes guide

findings.topic: AI — disengage conditions (does it give up?)
findings.detail: TWO hard disengage conditions. (1) SAFE ZONE: 'Once you cross the safe-zone boundary back into your garden, the guardian immediately stops pursuit and returns to its nest. The boundary is a hard disengage.' (2) DROPPING THE EGG: 'Drop the egg when a guardian closes in so it turns around and walks back, then pick the egg up and continue once it disengages.' The guardian's goal is the EGG, not the player — it is an object-retrieval AI wearing a chase costume. There is no gradual aggro decay, no search state, no last-known-position behavior.

findings.topic: AI — returns to nest and carries the egg back
findings.detail: On disengage or on a successful catch the guardian returns the egg to its nest, making that egg unstealable for the remainder of the cycle. Confirmed by the wall-drop exploit, which works precisely BECAUSE the guardian tries to reclaim: 'a boss cannot pull an egg out of a wall'. Server reset restores bosses to their nests.
findings.source: allthings.how boss-glitches article; sportskeeda summary ('the egg will go back to the nest, making it impossible to steal')

findings.detail: The guardian AI is a Roblox Pathfinding-service actor with documented failure modes: (1) it stalls out in tight corners and cannot grab an egg wedged in a confined space; (2) it cannot pull an egg out of a perimeter wall — players use this to shuttle eggs toward spawn in stages; (3) two players repeating a steal-and-drop cycle can 'break the area boss outright, wedging it into the ground or knocking it out of the map'; (4) all six tested boss types (chicken, duck, tiger, whale, dinosaur, Kitsune) 'respond identically to exploits, suggesting standardized AI behavior across encounters' — i.e. ONE shared AI script parameterized per biome, not bespoke behaviors.

Contact from the guardian ragdolls and LAUNCHES the player back to the start / away from the biome. 'Getting caught triggers a ragdoll that flings you away from the biome, costing the entire run. The egg you were carrying drops on the ground.' The egg is then reclaimed by the guardian and returned to its nest. The fling itself IS the punishment — a forced re-traversal of the whole map.
findings.source: games.gg biomes guide; allthings.how boss-glitches; eldorado.gg ('launched back toward the starting point empty-handed')

findings.topic: ON CATCH — no stun duration published
findings.detail: No source anywhere gives a stun/knockdown duration in seconds for being caught by a guardian. The mechanic is a physics ragdoll + positional reset rather than a timed stun lock. Searches specifically targeting stun duration returned explicit 'not specified' results across every guide.
findings.source: absence across games.gg, allthings.how, stealanegg.pro, techwiser, eldorado, sportskeeda, Fandom

findings.topic: ON CATCH — no money loss, no pet loss
findings.detail: No source mentions any currency penalty, pet loss, income penalty, or progress rollback on being caught. The only loss is the in-transit egg (and the time spent). Money is generated passively by pets in the pen and is untouched by the chase loop.
findings.source: absence of any money-penalty mention across all consulted sources

findings.topic: ON CATCH — multi-egg carry loses everything
findings.detail: stealanegg.pro states 'you lose ALL carried eggs, not just one', and advises 'single eggs only' from Abyss Ocean onward. Multi-egg carrying is implied to exist as a mechanic (guides repeatedly advise 'Stick to one egg per trip until your speed is well above the biome minimum'), which means carry count compounds the weight penalty AND the risk.

An on-screen 'RUN!!' warning appears the instant an egg is grabbed. This is the game's entire alarm UI: a single binary state flip from calm to chased. There is no meter, no suspicion bar, no escalating alert level.

findings.topic: TENSION — NO sight cone, NO noise system, NO grab timer
findings.detail: Exhaustive searching across Fandom, games.gg, allthings.how, eldorado, stealanegg.pro, techwiser, bloxron and Roblox's own description found ZERO mention of a vision cone, line-of-sight check, noise/sound-detection system, crouch/sneak input, or a countdown timer after grabbing an egg. The tension is entirely kinetic (a speed race over distance), not perceptual. This is the single most important design finding: the game deliberately has no stealth layer.
findings.source: systematic absence across all consulted sources

findings.topic: TENSION — 5-minute global reset cycle + 13-second map closure
findings.detail: 'Egg spawns reset every five minutes, and the map closes for 13 seconds between cycles.' The Fandom wiki confirms 'Egg Resets: the eggs reset every 5 minutes.' The 13-second lockout is a hard gate that resets everyone to a shared starting line each cycle — a deliberate race-start mechanic.

'A server announcement is made on top of the players screen as the egg spawns.' Broadcast format names both egg and biome, e.g. 'A Secret Cerberus egg spawned in Volcano' or 'A Secret Dragon egg has spawned in Cosmic'. All 7 players on a server share ONE egg pool — 'once someone carries a rare egg home, it disappears for that cycle.' This is the real tension generator: the announcement converts the whole 7-player server into a simultaneous footrace toward one nest, with the guardian as a shared obstacle and the other six players as the actual threat. Documented rare spawns: Secret Cerberus (Volcano), Kraken (Abyss Ocean), Eternal Ice Dragon (Snow), Eternal Mosasaurus (Prehistoric), Eternal Pterodactyl (Prehistoric), Secret Tralaledon (Prehistoric), Secret Dragon (Cosmic).

findings.topic: TENSION — night phase and forced teleport
findings.detail: A day/night cycle repeats 'every few minutes'. During night, pen egg growth applies at 30x. When the night countdown ENDS, anyone still outside the safe zone is force-teleported back to the starting area — punishing players camping far biomes like Prehistoric. Two glitches bypass it (Wi-Fi disconnect at the biome border; holding spacebar/jump on PC); a Volcano geometry pocket also survives the reset.
findings.source: allthings.how hidden-secrets article; allthings.how glitches article

findings.detail: From the Fandom Boosts page: 'Players can only interact with a bear trap if they're holding an egg, you can place max 3 down on the map. The owner can either pick them up or get it back when something steps in it, making them stuck for 7 seconds. You have an infinite supply of them and there is no known way to obtain more than 3. You can NOT place bear traps in the safe zone.' allthings.how independently reports the lock at FIVE seconds. Traps affect both pursuing guardians and rival players. Trap chaining (placing sequentially) is advised to extend crowd control.
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Boosts (read directly); allthings.how bat-and-traps article ('held in place for five seconds')

findings.detail: A melee weapon used against PLAYERS, not guardians. 'Each biome has its own bat that unlocks once you complete that biome's pets in the index. Fill out the Lake pets and you unlock the Lake bat, complete the Desert pets for the Desert bat, the Jungle pets for the Jungle bat.' 'The bat's power scales with rarity, so the higher the rarity you complete in the index, the harder your bat hits.' Effect: 'The hit ragdolls the player and flings them off course', making them drop the carried egg; press E to pick the egg up. A Bee Gun exists, unlocked by completing the limited-egg index. No cooldown published.
findings.source: allthings.how/how-to-use-the-bat-and-bear-traps-in-steal-an-egg-roblox/; allthings.how hidden-secrets article; stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Cosmic_Skeleton_Boss ('use the bat to knock out other players before stealing the egg')

findings.topic: COUNTERPLAY — NO stealth, invisibility, smoke, or stamina
findings.detail: There is no invisibility item, no smoke bomb, no distraction/decoy item, no sprint button, no stamina bar, and no hiding spots as a designed system. 'Speed' is a persistent trained STAT (a number in the millions/billions), not a burst resource. Gamepasses are purely economic: X2 Growth Speed (467 Robux), X2 Money (399 Robux), Grow All Eggs (~160 Robux per use), Instant Hatch (~9 Robux per use) — 'None of these gamepasses relate to speed boosts for player movement, protection mechanics, or PvP combat.' Hiding exists only as GLITCHES (the Cherry Blossom incubator hide, now patched with a blocking part; the Volcano geometry pocket).
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Gamepasses; allthings.how gamepasses article; allthings.how glitches article

findings.topic: COUNTERPLAY — Speed stat: Treadmills and Trails
findings.detail: Speed is the ONLY real counterplay axis. TREADMILLS (training multiplier, 10 tiers): base 2x, Sci-Fi 5x, Flame 12x, Celebrity 30x, Golden 80x, The Freeze 100x, Lucky Block 200x, Hacker 500x, Demonic 1,000x, Angelic 2,000x. TRAILS (direct movement multiplier, one equipped at a time, 10 tiers with costs): Grey COMMON 1.5x ($100), Green UNCOMMON 2x ($5,000), Blue RARE 2.5x ($75,000), Purple EPIC 3x ($1,500,000), Golden LEGENDARY 3.5x ($30,000,000), Red MYTHIC 4x ($750,000,000), Galaxy COSMIC 5x ($20,000,000,000), Secret SECRET 7x ($500,000,000,000), Eternal ETERNAL 10x ($12,500,000,000,000), Divine DIVINE 14x ($300,000,000,000,000). Free 10,000 Speed for liking + favoriting the game + joining the group. Speed also purchasable with Robux.

findings.topic: COUNTERPLAY — egg size is the anti-speed tax
findings.detail: Egg size is a risk/reward dial: bigger egg = bigger income multiplier on the hatched pet, but heavier carry and slower movement. 'The larger the egg, the higher the value multiplier applied to the animal inside it. But above all, it will be heavier, and you will be slower.' Reported figures: Giant eggs cut sprint speed by ~50%; some eggs weigh up to 90,000kg. Consequence: 'a biome you can clear with a small egg may still catch you out with a large one', and 'a player carrying a huge egg at exactly the minimum speed will still lose that egg regularly.' Size multipliers seen in worked examples: Giant x3, Huge x5.
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Eggs and /wiki/Mutations; eldorado.gg; games.gg biomes guide

findings.detail: Two contradictory recommendations exist. stealanegg.pro / allthings.how: 'Run laterally in a zigzag instead of straight lines, weaving around bushes and terrain, since the pursuit AI struggles to land hits on a side-to-side path.' games.gg / eldorado: 'Avoid running a curved or zig-zag path back to base, as this bleeds momentum and hands the pursuer ground it would never gain on a straight line.' Likely resolution: zigzagging beats the guardian's HIT registration but loses the SPEED race, so it only helps when you are marginally faster and being nipped at, not when you are slower.
findings.source: stealanegg.pro and allthings.how vs games.gg and eldorado.gg

findings.detail: Universal community rule of thumb: bring roughly DOUBLE the listed biome minimum before farming it. Cherry Blossom's listed 2,500,000,000 has a practical threshold reported 'closer to 3.5 billion' — around 3.5B+ Speed 'is a better target if you want to consistently farm Cherry Blossom Eggs and avoid being caught by guardian Pets.' The listed number is entry/gate speed; the escape speed with a loaded egg is materially higher.
findings.source: games.gg biomes guide; eldorado.gg; stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Zones tip ('Having enough Speed to enter a zone does not necessarily mean you have enough Speed to safely return with a large Egg')

findings.topic: SCALING — the only published guardian scaling axis is speed gates
findings.detail: Guardian difficulty is expressed exclusively as the biome's Speed requirement. The curve: 0 → 900 → 10K → 40K → 170K → 700K → 2.5M → 17-18M → 700M → 2.5B → 7B. Step multipliers between tiers: Lake→Desert ~11x, Desert→Jungle 4x, Jungle→Snow ~4.3x, Snow→Volcano ~4.1x, Volcano→Abyss ~3.6x, Abyss→Prehistoric ~6.8x, Prehistoric→Cosmic ~41x (the single biggest wall in the game), Cosmic→Cherry Blossom ~3.6x, Cherry Blossom→Titan Temple 2.8x. NO guardian HP, damage, chase-speed value, aggro radius, or attack rate is published anywhere — because none appear to be surfaced in-game.
findings.source: stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Zones; eldorado.gg; allthings.how; steal-an-eggwiki.wiki (all agree on the ladder)

findings.topic: SCALING — Jungle and Prehistoric values disputed
findings.detail: Jungle is listed as 40,000 by Fandom, games.gg, eldorado and allthings.how, but 'has also been reported as high as 50,000' (allthings.how). Prehistoric is listed as 17,000,000 by allthings.how and steal-an-eggwiki.wiki but 18,000,000 by games.gg and eldorado; the Fandom wiki hedges with '~17,000,000–18,000,000' and explicitly notes 'Some sources disagree on exact values, particularly for Jungle and Prehistoric.'

'Anyone in the server can bat the egg out of your hands on the way back.' 'Other players can steal an egg directly from you while you're carrying it back... if you spot someone carrying a better egg than anything available at the nest, intercepting them is a legitimate strategy.' 'A guardian defends its own biome, but rival players are free to attack you ANYWHERE on the map.' Advanced tactic: 'predict their route home and wait near the guardian' to ambush the second-place racer. Both PvP tools are 'offensive by nature', offering no protection while carrying.
findings.source: bloxron.com/steal-an-egg; games.gg beginner guide; allthings.how bat-and-traps; stealaneggguide.wiki

findings.topic: PVP — bases and pens are INVIOLABLE
findings.detail: 'Once the egg is placed in your base's hatching area, it is safe from other players.' 'While eggs and pets are actively being transported across the map, they can be intercepted by other players, but once safely placed in your base, they are protected.' 'There is no legitimate route to receive a pet from someone else' — everything on your base must come from hatching, stealing (in transit) or fusing. There is NO base raiding of hatched pets. The safe zone is also where bear traps cannot be placed and where guardians hard-disengage. The 'steal from other players' in the official description refers exclusively to in-transit interception.
findings.source: allthings.how bat-and-traps article; games.gg beginner guide; allthings.how pet-dupe article

findings.topic: PVP — no cooldowns, no protection timers, no revenge system documented
findings.detail: No source documents a PvP cooldown, an attack cooldown on the bat, a grace period after being hit, a raid cooldown, spawn protection, or any revenge/bounty/retaliation mechanic. The only structural limiter is the 3-trap placement cap. Absence is consistent across every consulted source including the Fandom wiki.
findings.source: systematic absence across Fandom, allthings.how, games.gg, bloxron, eldorado, stealaneggguide.wiki

findings.topic: UNRELIABLE SOURCE WARNING — fabricated base-defense systems
findings.detail: stealanegg.pro claims 'Rival players can raid your base garden if security defenses are weak; upgrading the Security Defense Wall deters thieves.' A summary of LOLGA content claims an upgrade order of 'Treadmill → Base Income Multiplier → Walls → Alarms → Turrets'. NEITHER is corroborated by the Fandom wiki, the official Roblox description, or any other source, and both directly contradict the well-attested 'pen is safe' rule. Treat walls/alarms/turrets/security-defense-wall as SEO fabrication, not game content.
findings.source: stealanegg.pro/guide/how-to-steal-eggs and lolga.com, contradicted by stealanegg.fandom.com and roblox.com description

findings.topic: UNRELIABLE SOURCE WARNING — fabricated boss-fight combat system
findings.detail: steal-an-eggwiki.wiki/guide/steal-an-egg-boss-fight/ describes boss HP pools (Tier 1: 100k-500k HP, Tier 2: 10M-50M, Tier 3: 100M-500M, Tier 4: 1B+), 'AOE attacks', 'enrage timers', and 'boss damage reduction shields'. NONE of this exists — there is no combat against guardians in Steal An Egg at all; guardians cannot be fought, only outrun, trapped or glitched. This page is machine-generated filler and should be disregarded entirely.

findings.topic: Design takeaway — the whole tension model in one line
findings.detail: Steal An Egg's guardian system is a SINGLE binary event, not a state machine: sleep → (player grabs egg) → straight-line chase at a fixed speed → resolved by a stat comparison → hard disengage at the safe-zone line. There is no perception layer, no alert escalation, no search behavior, no timer. All the felt tension is loaded into (a) the 5-minute reset race, (b) the server-wide rare-egg broadcast, (c) the egg-size greed/weight tradeoff, and (d) six other players who can bat you at any moment. The guardian is a difficulty gate wearing an animal costume; the PLAYERS are the actual antagonists.

MUTATIONS (income multipliers, rolled at hatch): Rainbow x3.5 (roll weight 1/100), Parasite x3 (feeding-event exclusive), Golden x2.5 (4/100), Spirit Bloom x2.5 (Sakura Incubator only), Bloom x1.25 (Sakura event), Silver x1.2 (6/100). Final Income = Base × Color Multiplier × Size Multiplier. CHERRY BLOSSOM EVENT: 'Great Bloom' fires every 30 minutes, spawning Sakura Crystal Trees to smash for crystals that charge the Sakura Incubator (low charge rolls Bloom, full charge guarantees Spirit Bloom; charge decays if idle). TITAN TEMPLE / 'Monsters Are Coming' (Update 2, Aug 29-30 2026): added the Hungry Frog event — find infected/parasite eggs, bring them home to remove the Parasite, feed 5 Parasites to the Hungry Frog for one Monster Chest. Divine eggs have a 16-hour hatch time. Each biome holds 8 eggs/pets (Desert and Cherry Blossom list 7).

openQuestions: Exact guardian movement speeds are unpublished — no source gives a studs/sec or Speed-stat equivalent for any guardian, only the player-side entry thresholds. Determining whether the guardian's speed is a flat value per biome or scales relative to the player's Speed stat would require decompiling the game or in-game testing.

Whether a proximity detection radius exists at all. Every mention traces back to one SEO aggregator (stealanegg.pro) with no numbers. The Fandom 'guardians sleep next to their nests' description plus the aggro-on-pickup trigger suggests it does NOT — but this needs in-game confirmation.
Bear trap lock duration: Fandom says 7 seconds, allthings.how says 5 seconds. Unresolved. Possibly 5s vs players and 7s vs guardians, or one source is stale after a balance patch.

Whether guardians can be trapped by bear traps at all — sources say traps 'slow a pursuing Guardian' and also that they hold 'any player who walks over it'; whether the effect and duration differ for NPCs is unstated.
Bat cooldown / swing rate and whether bat power is a discrete tier per biome index completed or a continuous scalar. No numbers published.
Whether multi-egg carrying is a real mechanic with a cap, or whether guides advising 'one egg per trip' are describing repeat trips. The 'you lose ALL carried eggs' claim is single-sourced.

Guardian visual designs for Abyss Ocean, Prehistoric, Cosmic, Cherry Blossom and Titan Temple — no art exists on the wiki (files return 'missing') and no other source describes them. Would need in-game screenshots or YouTube gameplay frames.
Cherry Blossom guardian's canonical name (Nine-Tailed Fox / Kitsune / Oni Tiger / Mother Crane) — four different names across four sources, unresolved by any first-party source.

Whether the Volcano guardian is genuinely a hellhound/Cerberus. The wiki's own VolcanoGuardian.png reads as a lava dragon/drake in profile, not a three-headed dog, contradicting the name used by every text source.
Exact day/night cycle period. Sources say night growth is 30x and repeats 'every few minutes' but no one gives the actual cycle length or the night window duration.

Whether there is any developer-published documentation (Discord announcements, Trello, patch notes) with real tuning values — the game has an official Discord and Roblox Group linked from the wiki that were not accessible in this pass.

summary:
The Steal An Egg pet index runs 11 biomes in progression order: Forest → Lake → Desert → Jungle → Snow → Volcano → Abyss Ocean → Prehistoric → Cosmic → Cherry Blossom → Titan Temple, plus an "Event" pool of shop/limited pets. Rarity ladder: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Cosmic, Secret, Eternal, Divine (+Event). Roughly 88 biome pets + 18 limited = ~106 total.

The single most valuable source found was the wiki's raw Lua data module (https://stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Module:Pets/Data?action=raw), which yields authoritative biome + rarity + income for ~99 pets. It cross-validates almost perfectly against Eldorado, timesaver.gg and allthings.how. One pet, Oni Tiger (Eternal, Cherry Blossom, $600M/s), is absent from the module but confirmed by the Cherry Blossom zone page and Eldorado.

Highest incomes: Mecha Dreadscale $4B/s (limited Mecha variant) > Nightflame $3B/s (Divine, Titan Temple) > Dreadscale $2B/s > Kitsune $1.8B/s > Unicorn = Mecha Krakenoid $1B/s > Gorilla King $880M/s (best farmable) > Mecha Crocodon $680M/s > Oni Tiger $600M/s > Krakenoid $500M/s.

Only three Divine biome pets exist: Unicorn (Cosmic, 700M speed), Kitsune (Cherry Blossom, 2.5B speed), Nightflame (Titan Temple, 7B speed). Eleven Secret pets, eight Eternal.

Drop chances: no official % exist for biome Secret/Eternal/Divine pets — they appear as a single server-announced rare egg per ~5-minute reset, shared among all 7 players. Published odds exist only for the two Robux eggs: Brainrot Egg (Tung Tung Sahur 39% → Strawberry Elephant 1%) and Monster Egg (Scorpio 39% → Dreadscale 0.5%, each Mecha variant 1%).

For visuals, I rendered the actual wiki artwork in-browser and directly observed 27 late-game pets — those descriptions are OBSERVED and modeling-ready. The art style splits into two families: chunky voxel/Minecraft-like builds (Cerberus, Kraken, Tralaledon, Snowy Owl, Ankylosaurus, Centapede, Cosmic Gorilla, Unicorn) and smooth stylized low-poly (Kitsune, Stag, Oni Tiger, Koi, Red Panda, Salamander, Crane, Mantaris, Crustacia). Remaining pets' visuals are marked INFERRED.

findings.detail: The Fandom wiki's Lua data module at https://stealanegg.fandom.com/wiki/Module:Pets/Data?action=raw returns the complete pet table as structured data (rarity → pet name → biome, image, income). This is the single best machine-readable source. WebFetch gets HTTP 402 on stealanegg.fandom.com; the page must be reached via a real browser. The rendered /wiki/Pets gallery is script-broken but its filter chips work.

11 biomes in order: Forest, Lake, Desert, Jungle, Snow, Volcano, Abyss Ocean, Prehistoric, Cosmic, Cherry Blossom, Titan Temple. Speed requirements for late-game: Cosmic 700,000,000; Cherry Blossom 2,500,000,000; Titan Temple 7,000,000,000. Guardians: Cosmic Guardian (Cosmic), Nine-Tailed Fox (Cherry Blossom), Gorilla King (Titan Temple). Titan Temple was added in Update #2, Aug 2026 ('Monsters Are Coming', weekend of Aug 29-30 2026); Cherry Blossom in Update #1, Aug 22 2026.

Broad barrel chest bears a large glowing cyan/teal starburst emblem — a radiant crystalline eight-point flare with spiked rays casting light onto the surrounding fur. Short ape-like muzzle, two glowing cyan slit eyes, small pointed horn-ears. Thick digitigrade legs, clawed feet. Effects: cyan emissive bloom from chest and eyes, dark smoke wisps. findings.detail: Creature: nine-tailed fox / multi-headed spirit fox. VISUAL (OBSERVED): pale ivory-to-bone-cream fur, smooth low-poly. Bold dark-crimson brush-stroke tribal swirls painted across each muzzle, forehead and the flanks — Japanese oni/fox-mask motif with hooked spiral strokes. Eyes glow hot orange-amber. Muzzle tips and paws are dark charcoal-grey. Tall pointed ears with darker inner shading. Multiple bushy tails fan behind. Quadruped, slender canine build. Requires 2.5B speed.

Creature: unicorn/horse. VISUAL (OBSERVED): deliberately blocky Roblox-primitive construction — rectangular slab body, four plain cylindrical/box legs, box head. Body is soft pastel pink / light magenta with flat unshaded faces. Mane and tail are bright saturated lemon-yellow, blocky, sculpted into stepped rectangular tufts. A single large spiral horn in bright yellow-gold projects forward and up from the forehead. Simple small dark dot eyes. Reads as a candy-colored toy horse — noticeably cruder/blockier than the other Divines. Requires 700M speed.

Creature: crowned silverback gorilla; also the Titan Temple biome Guardian. VISUAL (OBSERVED): massive matte-black-furred gorilla in a knuckle-forward stance, mouth wide open in a roar showing white teeth and a pink tongue. Wears a spiked GOLD CROWN on the head, gold arm-bands/bracers on both wrists, and a gold shoulder-and-chest harness with a plate over the sternum. Face and chest fur slightly lighter grey than the body. Exaggerated proportions: enormous shoulders and arms, small stubby legs, broad flat nose, deep brow ridge. A single large pale-grey/bone horn juts forward from the snout, with smaller spikes over the brow and along the back. Pale grey hooves/claws. Long thick tail with a spiked ridge. Quadruped, head lowered in a charging stance. Effects: orange emissive glow along the cracks, ember particles.

Creature: giant praying mantis. VISUAL (OBSERVED): upright bipedal mantis. Bright leaf-green segmented armored torso with lighter lime plating banding the abdomen. Two large translucent green wings spread wide behind it, leaf-veined and slightly darker at the edges. Triangular head with big glowing VIOLET/PURPLE compound eyes and two thin black antennae. Raptorial forelimbs raised in a striking pose; four thin spindly legs below.

Creature: long bladed-spine reptile (monitor lizard / crocodilian). VISUAL (OBSERVED): low quadruped with a very long tapering tail nearly twice the body length. Steel blue-grey scaled body with a paler ice-blue underside and throat. A SERRATED RIDGE OF BLADE-LIKE SCALES runs the full length of the spine from skull to tail tip, each scale a flat triangular fin. Short splayed legs with clawed feet, elongated narrow snout, small dark eye.

Creature: crab/lobster. VISUAL (OBSERVED): striking silhouette — TWO ENORMOUS FAN-SHAPED CRESCENT CLAWS raised high on either side like wings, each in dark blood-red/maroon with a textured, ridged, honeycombed shell surface and darker outline. The central body/head is small by comparison, dark navy-purple, with two small glowing RED eyes. Two long thin antennae curl down and outward from the face like whiskers. Overall reads like a demonic moth or manta because the claws dominate the shape.

Creature: giant tarantula. VISUAL (OBSERVED): eight long angular legs arched high above a low body. Abdomen and cephalothorax are bronze/tan-gold with banded plate markings; the legs are darker brown-black and segmented. A CLUSTER OF GLOWING VIOLET/PURPLE EYES sits at the front of the head, with a purple gem-like marking on the back plate. Slightly hairy, faceted low-poly surface.

Creature: three-headed hellhound. VISUAL (OBSERVED): blocky voxel build. THREE IDENTICAL HEADS sit side by side on one broad neck. Body is dark charcoal-navy; the chest, forelegs and all three muzzles are lighter grey-lavender. EACH of the three heads is crowned with a crest of bright ORANGE-AND-RED VOXEL FLAMES rising like a burning mane. Small dark eyes with red glints. Squat sturdy four-legged proportions with cube paws. Effects: flickering fire particles above all three heads.

Six-to-eight thick tentacles splay outward and curl forward and down, each built from tapering cube segments with visible sucker nubs. Uniform saturated red with darker red shading underneath. findings.topic: Secret pet drop chances — no official odds exist
findings.detail: There are NO published drop percentages for any biome Secret, Eternal or Divine pet. The mechanic is not a per-egg roll: ONE rare egg spawns per server per ~5-minute egg reset, is announced server-wide by name and biome, and is contested by all 7 players in the server. Relative rarity by badge counts is Divine (rarest) > Eternal > Secret. Speed gates by Secret: King Snake ~40,000 (lowest); Yeti ~170,000; Cerberus ~700,000 (Volcano); Kraken ~2,500,000; T-Rex/Tralaledon ~17-18M; Cosmic Skeleton Boss & Cosmic Dragon 700,000,000; Stag 2,500,000,000; Mutant Shark 7,000,000,000. Final Income = Base Income × Colour (mutation) Multiplier × Size Multiplier. Confirmed multipliers: Silver 1.25x, Bloom 1.5x, Golden 2x, Rainbow 2.5x, Spirit Bloom 3x. The roster splits into two distinct visual families, and this is the single most useful modelling note. (1) CHUNKY VOXEL / Minecraft-like: built from visible stacked cubes with flat unshaded faces — Cerberus, Kraken, Tralaledon, Snowy Owl, Ankylosaurus, Centapede, Cosmic Gorilla, Unicorn, T-Rex. (2) SMOOTH STYLIZED LOW-POLY: soft rounded forms, gradient shading, expressive faces — Kitsune, Stag, Oni Tiger, Koi, Red Panda, Salamander, Crane, Mantaris, Crustacia, Gorilla King, Nightflame, Rhinotaur, Bladehide, Spideron. Newer biomes (Cherry Blossom, Titan Temple) skew almost entirely to family 2, which suggests the art direction shifted mid-development. Recurring effect motifs: glowing molten-crack emissives on Volcano/Titan pets, white star-speck sparkles on Cosmic pets, and magenta/red mask-and-swirl tattooing on Cherry Blossom pets.

summary:
Steal An Egg (Roblox) pet index — first half (Forest → Abyss Ocean, 56 of ~106 pets), with income, rarity, biome and artist-grade visual descriptions derived from the actual in-game model renders on the official Fandom wiki (downloaded from the wikia CDN and inspected directly, not guessed).

STRUCTURE: 11 biomes + limited/event eggs. Zones unlock by SPEED stat: Forest (0) → Lake (900) → Desert (10,000) → Jungle (40,000) → Snow (170,000) → Volcano (700,000) → Abyss Ocean (2,500,000) → Prehistoric (18M) → Cosmic (700M) → Cherry Blossom (2.5B) → Titan Temple. Each biome holds exactly 8 pets, one per rarity rung, and is patrolled by a sleeping Guardian (Forest=Chicken, Lake=Swan, Desert=Scorpion, Jungle=Tiger, Snow=Yeti, Volcano=Cerberus, Prehistoric=T-Rex, Cosmic=Cosmic Skeleton Boss). Eggs respawn every 5 minutes.

RARITIES (10): Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Cosmic, Secret, Eternal, Divine. Card-background colors confirmed from in-game screenshots: Common = charcoal grey, Rare = blue gradient, Epic = purple/magenta gradient, Mythic = crimson gradient. Higher-tier colors unconfirmed.

MUTATIONS (Fandom wiki, with roll weights out of 100): Rainbow x3.5 (weight 1), Parasite x3 (Parasite Egg / feeding event only), Golden x2.5 (weight 4), Spirit Bloom x2.5 (Sakura Incubator, full charge), Bloom x1.25 (Sakura Incubator, partial charge), Silver x1.2 (weight 6). Third-party guides publish a conflicting weaker set (Silver 1.25 / Bloom 1.5 / Golden 2 / Rainbow 2.5 / Spirit Bloom 3) — flagged. IMPORTANT: there are no Diamond or Neon mutations in this game, and no Titanic size; those belong to other Roblox pet titles.

SIZE: an independent trait shown as a raw WEIGHT IN KG on the pet card, rolled separately from color. Named rolls include Tiny, Giant (x3) and Huge (x5). Egg size at pickup drives it: Small 1.0x / Normal 1.2x / Large 1.5x / Huge 2.0x / Giant 3.0x, with escalating carry-speed penalties (0% to -50%). Final Income = Base Income × Color Multiplier × Size Multiplier.

ART STYLE: Roblox voxel construction — cubes with visible square stud/panel indentations, a thick black toon outline on every pet, flat saturated 2-3 tone colors, chunky big-head proportions, dot or oval eyes with a white specular square. Late-tier pets shift to a smoother faceted low-poly look. Critically, each pet ships in multiple color variants that change appearance but NOT income.
