findings.detail: Bloom and Spirit Bloom are applied post-hatch, not rolled. Steps: unlock Cherry Blossom biome (2.5B speed), collect Sakura Crystals from the biome to charge the incubator, place a pet inside, then charge. A lower charge rolls a chance at Bloom; a full charge guarantees Spirit Bloom. Charge decays if the incubator sits idle, so crystals must be fed steadily rather than banked.

Beyond hatching, mutations come from fusing (combining three pets with identical mutations yields a mutated offspring, carrying the bonus through tier progression) and from Admin Abuse events held on Saturdays, which offer Silver, Golden and Rainbow chances.

Size is an independent trait from color mutation, rolled separately at hatch and displayed as a raw WEIGHT IN KG on the pet card (not a tier label). This is why the same pet can appear as a Golden Giant, or as a plain Huge with no color mutation at all. Named rolls referenced: Tiny (grants speed utility and faster hatch time), Giant (x3 multiplier on both cash and speed bonus), Huge (x5). Observed real weights vary enormously by species: Phoenix 2,747kg, Cerberus 10,115kg, a BIG King Mammoth 5,583,559kg.

The egg's physical size at pickup determines the pet's size multiplier: Small 1.0x (~60% spawn, no speed penalty), Normal 1.2x (~25%, -5%), Large 1.5x (~10%, -15%), Huge 2.0x (~4%, -30%), Giant 3.0x (<1%, -50%). Bigger egg = bigger payout but heavier carry and slower escape, which is the core risk/reward loop. Note this Giant 3.0x table conflicts slightly with the Fandom worked example implying Huge = x5.

Final Income = Base Income × Color Multiplier × Size Multiplier. Mutations and size stack multiplicatively and independently. Worked examples from the wiki: base $100/s; Golden + Giant = 100 × 2.5 × 3 = $750/s (x7.5 total); Rainbow + Huge = 100 × 3.5 × 5 = $1,750/s (x17.5 total). A mutated Common can out-earn an unmutated Rare.

There is no Diamond mutation, no Neon mutation, and no Titanic size in Steal An Egg. Those belong to other Roblox pet titles (Pet Simulator, Adopt Me, Pets Go). Searches specifically for Titanic/Colossal in this game returned only cross-game noise. The size vocabulary here is Tiny / Small / Normal / Large / Huge / Giant plus a kg weight number.
findings.source: Negative result across WebSearch for Titanic/Colossal/Diamond/Neon + Steal an Egg

findings.detail: The wiki states all eggs come in different colors, and these colors change the appearance of BOTH the egg and the hatched pet — but do NOT change income. Players are told to judge value by the egg's SHAPE, not its color. For a 3D artist this means every pet needs a base mesh with a swappable palette, not a single fixed texture.

Roblox voxel construction: bodies assembled from axis-aligned cubes with visible square stud/panel indentations pressed into each face. Every pet carries a thick black cartoon outline (toon shader rim). Colors are flat and saturated with only 2-3 shading tones per material. Proportions are chunky — oversized head relative to body, short thick limbs, wide stable stance. Faces are minimal: black dot or oval eyes, often with a single white specular highlight square, plus a simple mouth line. A typical blocky quadruped reads as 8-14 primitive boxes. Later/premium tier pets (King Snake, Kitsune, Koi, Red Panda, Crane, Stag) shift to a smoother faceted low-poly style rather than pure cubes.

summary:
Steal An Egg (Roblox universe 10563114921 / place 107778070777162, by verified group "and Collect Rare Pets", created 2026-07-25, ~1.37B visits, ~1.5M CCU, 7-player servers, Simulation/Tycoon) is visually a "Roblox blocky-plus" game, NOT smooth low-poly. Terrain, props and architecture are classic axis-aligned Roblox Parts with visible studs and tiled textures (checkerboard grass, stud grids, plank/brick fences). Creatures — both pets and biome guardians — are overwhelmingly blocky voxel builds of 8-20 stacked boxes with painted faces; only a minority (and the marketing thumbnails) use faceted smooth low-poly. Materials are matte plastic with no PBR; Neon is used for lava, trails, hatch bursts and glow rings. Lighting is a single fixed bright day, high sun, soft low-contrast shadows, mild bloom, no fog (you can see across biome boundaries), no day/night cycle, no DOF or motion blur. Saturation is extreme and comes from albedo, not grading.

Eleven biomes run in a fixed line on one flat plane, each a walled corridor: Forest, Lake, Desert, Jungle, Snow, Volcano, Abyss Ocean, Prehistoric, Cosmic, Cherry Blossom, Titan Temple. Each has a distinct near-primary palette and a sleeping guardian beside twig-bowl nests.

The HUD is sparse and corner-anchored: green "Shop" and blue "Index" pills on the left with a "Slow Mode" toggle; two thick gold-bordered squares (red egg, tan paw) on the right; Speed (cyan escalating to magenta, with an "(x1K)" multiplier) and Money (green) stacked bottom-left; an egg-reset countdown bottom-right; Roblox's default hotbar bottom-centre; Roblox's UNMODIFIED dark PlayerList top-right as the leaderboard (columns People / Speed / Money/s). There is NO minimap and NO persistent quest tracker — only a single centred white objective line. There is no steal beam; stealing is a proximity "E" prompt plus a white SelectionBox highlight.

All UI text uses a heavy rounded display face (Fredoka/Luckiest Guy class) with 2-4px black outlines. Panels are dark charcoal rounded rects with overhanging titles and red rounded-square X buttons. Menus: Pet Index (biome rows of 8 rarity-coloured tiles, silhouettes for undiscovered, claim rewards, 1/78), Robux Shop, Speed Shop, Trail Shop (magenta gradient header, horizontally scrolling gradient cards), Fuse Machine, Free Gift, and event popups.

findings.detail: Chibi-adjacent but not extreme big-head chibi — closest to Minecraft-mob proportions: an oversized boxy head on quadrupeds, stubby cuboid legs, no neck, minimal silhouette detail. Faces are painted decals or small contrasting blocks (dot eyes, simple mouths).
Pets stand roughly half to two-thirds the height of an R15 Roblox character, on the ground. Late-game pets (sharks, dragons, gorillas) are considerably larger. Guardians are 3-8x player height.

Common pets read as ~120-400 triangles (each box = 12 tris; 10-20 boxes plus a few wedges). Mid/late pets read ~400-1,500 tris. Guardians read ~1,000-3,000 tris. Marketing-render creatures (faceted low-poly snake, T-Rex) read ~800-2,000 tris and are higher fidelity than shipped models. These are visual estimates from silhouette and facet counts, not extracted geometry.
findings.source: Visual estimation from full-res frames and store renders

findings.detail: Pen pets are STATIC placed income units — they stand in fixed spots on the grass and no walk cycle, idle bob, orbit or follow-the-player float was observed in ~25 minutes of footage. There is no classic pet-simulator following-pet system visible; animation energy goes into the floating '+$N' money popups above each pet instead. Guardians ARE animated — they sleep, wake and chase during the RUN!! state.

(a) Nest eggs: small, simple smooth/low-poly ovoids sitting in the nest — cream/white, pale blue, yellow — with simple decals (e.g. a white snowflake for Snow). (b) Carried eggs: LARGE, 2-3x player height, chunky VOXELISED ovoids built from stacked blocks with visible stepping, hoisted overhead by the player while running.
findings.source: Frames f_006, k_041, k_036; store screenshots

findings.detail: Solid base colour plus a motif: horizontal/diagonal banding (orange shell with dark brown bands = snake egg); plate-and-spike (T-Rex egg is dark brown with tan hexagonal scale plates and protruding bone spikes, top cracked open); speckle-and-sparkle (Cosmic egg is purple-magenta with cyan speckles and a glowing cyan-white star sparkle). Snow eggs carry a white snowflake emblem.
findings.source: Store screenshots store1.png, store2.png, store3.png, store4.png

findings.detail: The mutation is shown on the SHELL before pickup so players can spot it from a distance. Five mutations with multipliers: Silver 1.25x, Bloom 1.5x, Golden 2x, Rainbow 2.5x, Spirit Bloom 3x. Rainbow renders as a full vertical rainbow gradient shell (red-orange-yellow-green-blue-purple) over the base emblem. Silver, Golden and Rainbow spawn naturally in any biome; Bloom and Spirit Bloom come only from the Sakura Incubator in Cherry Blossom.
findings.source: games.gg mutations guide; visually confirmed rainbow shell in store3.png

findings.detail: Eggs grow in the nest through visible stages — an intermediate stage renders as a green leafy/blocky mass with small green gem shapes and red dots. When complete an 'Egg / Ready!' billboard appears above it ('Egg' in gold, 'Ready!' in white, both black-outlined). A right-side 'Growing Eggs' tracker panel lists each egg with a countdown and a green Ready pill.
findings.source: Frames f_006, f_014; sheet4_2 Growing Eggs panel

findings.detail: Size is separate from rarity and mutation and is displayed as a WEIGHT IN KILOGRAMS on the pet's world label (observed: '686Kg' in small grey text beside the pet). Mutation and size multipliers stack independently.

A low bowl/torus of chunky brown twig blocks radiating outward, sitting on a flat tan/pink dirt disc, roughly 6-10 studs wide, holding 1-3 eggs. Biome variants: bright golden-yellow woven straw (Snow), terracotta/red overlapping flat plates (Prehistoric), pale straw (Prehistoric secondary), grey stone basket (Volcano).

A rectangular fenced paddock on bright green grass. Fence = 2-3 orange-red horizontal rails with dark brown/near-black square posts and lighter caps; neighbouring player plots use white fences. Plot boundary is marked by a bright red/magenta line painted on the ground. Pets are placed loosely across the grass inside.

SELL stall (red-and-white striped awning on wooden posts, floating red 'SELL' sign); Fuse Machine (bright blue blocky body, dark grey cylinder smokestacks, white screen face with a black '?', light grey concrete pad, blue-white gradient 'Fuse Machine 0/3' label); Treadmill (black deck with white chevron arrows on the belt, side rails); Upgrade Pen plaque and a large magenta 3D billboard version; Trails Shop wooden pergola with a gold floating sign; a red 'FREE!' gift box with a yellow ribbon; 'Unlock: $1K' plot sign with a green/red price bar; and large white 3D block letters spelling SAFE ZONE lying on the ground with a blue shield icon.
findings.source: Frames f_028, g_012, h_012; sheet2_1, sheet4_1

findings.detail: The treadmill has a VERTICAL 'phone screen' panel mounted above it that plays a scrolling short-form video feed (dogs, nature clips) with large white left/right triangle arrow buttons on either side and heart/like icons down the right edge — a doomscrolling joke. A yellow '+2/step' popup fires per stride and green '+$N Speed' popups accumulate.

Roblox's native unibar (Roblox logo, hamburger menu, chat with an unread count badge, microphone), followed by two custom circular dark buttons ~36px: one emote/animation-style button and a settings gear. Exact function of the custom pair is not confirmed.

A single centred tutorial/objective line in white chunky bold, roughly 34px, with a heavy black outline and NO background plate. Observed strings: 'Steal an Egg!', 'Go to your Pen!', 'Place your Pet', 'Upgrade your Pen!', 'Use your treadmill to become faster!'. This is the ONLY quest guidance in the HUD.

A red rounded pill roughly 275x65px centred at the top (~y=55 of 720), with a lighter red/pink inner stroke and a dark red outer stroke, containing 'RUN!!' in large white chunky bold with a black outline. Fires when a guardian wakes.

At roughly x=10, y=288-372 (of 1280x720): 'Shop' — a green rounded rect ~130x48px with a white shopping-cart icon and white bold text, a darker green bottom bevel and a black outline; 'Index' directly below — the same shape in blue with a white book/list icon, carrying a small red circular unread badge with a numeral. Below those sits a 'Slow Mode' toggle: a small rounded switch, green when on / dark grey when off, with a white bold black-outlined label.
findings.source: Full-res frames k_069, k_088, k_094, h_012

findings.detail: Two stacked rounded squares ~56px at roughly x=1215, y=290-415, each with a thick gold/tan border: a red square with a cream EGG icon (egg inventory, carries a red numeric badge) and an orange/tan square with a dark brown PAW icon (pet inventory).

Stacked at x≈10: SPEED — a cyan winged-sneaker icon with a small yellow '+' circle badge, then the value in heavy bold with a black outline, with the colour escalating by magnitude (cyan at low values, MAGENTA/pink at billions), followed by the boost multiplier '(x1K)' in bright green. Below it MONEY — a green cash-stack icon and the value in bright green bold with a black outline. Values use K/M/B/T suffixes (e.g. '139.2B (x1K)', '$6.8T').
findings.source: Full-res frames k_069, k_088, k_094, f_028

findings.topic: HUD — income per second is NOT an aggregate stat
findings.detail: There is no single aggregate income/sec readout in the HUD. Per-pet income is shown on each pet's world-space nameplate as '$5/s' in green, and the player's total appears only as a 'Money/s' column in the leaderboard. This is a notable departure from typical pet-tycoon HUDs.

Bottom-centre uses Roblox's DEFAULT hotbar — up to 10 dark translucent rounded slots with numeric hotkeys, small item thumbnails and 'xN' stack counts (carried eggs, tools, pets). Bottom-right shows the global egg-reset countdown: a white wing/comet icon plus 'in 4m 22s' in white bold with a black outline.

findings.topic: HUD — no minimap, no quest tracker
findings.detail: There is NO minimap anywhere in the interface, and no persistent quest/objective tracker panel — only the single centred objective line. Confirmed across all four videos and every biome.
findings.source: All sampled frames from BCMIHVA4FQM, 8d7Qrz7jDrU, VNJ6efnsCME, EhTftioY4Oo

findings.detail: The leaderboard is Roblox's UNMODIFIED default PlayerList at top-right — a dark translucent (~70% black) rounded rect with a small white '×' at top-left, a header row in small light-grey Roblox sans ('People | Speed | Money/s', column order varies between builds), player names in white and two numeric stat columns, thin row separators and a right scrollbar. It is NOT custom-skinned and does not use the game's display font.
findings.source: High-zoom crop crop_grow.png; frames k_036, k_069, k_088

findings.detail: A right-side panel (~x=980-1265, y=255-495) with a dark charcoal body, a ~4px GOLD/tan border and ~14px corners. Header is a light tan gradient band: '14/14 Active' in white chunky bold with heavy black outline on the left, and a red rounded '+1 EQUIP [$1T]' button on the right. Body is a scrolling list of rows, each a slightly lighter dark rounded rect containing a square thumbnail tile with a white radial sunburst backing and the pet's 3D render, then the pet name and income on one rarity-coloured line (e.g. 'Koi ($24.3M/s)' in purple/violet), then a red rounded 'Unequip' button. A bright green 'Equip Best' button sits below the panel; a small red '>' tab collapses it.
findings.source: High-zoom crop crop_equip.png from frame k_069

findings.detail: Modal dark charcoal rounded panel with a light grey stroke and drop shadow. The title 'Pet Index' sits OUTSIDE the panel, overhanging the top-left corner, in white chunky bold. A red rounded-square X overhangs the top-right. The body is a vertical scroll of BIOME ROWS: each row begins with a biome card showing a painted/photographic biome thumbnail with the biome name overlaid in white bold ('Forest', 'Lake'), followed by 8 pet tiles. Tiles are rounded squares filled with a solid saturated colour (grey, green, blue, magenta, yellow, purple); undiscovered tiles show a BLACK SILHOUETTE with '???' in small white text, discovered tiles show the pet in full colour with its name. Beneath each row: a coloured progress dot, '3/8', and a small reward-item icon.

findings.topic: Menu — Pet Index right column and progress
findings.detail: The right column holds a large selected-pet preview card (dark rounded rect, light border) showing the pet model or silhouette, its name, its rarity in white/grey bold, and its income in green. Below sits a 'Rewards:' box with a dark green fill and a bright green stroke containing reward icons (a blue sneaker '+420' speed and a green cash stack '$100'), then a large 'CLAIM!' button — grey/white gradient when locked, green when ready, and 'CLAIMED!' in grey with green checkmarks over the icons once taken. The panel footer reads 'Unlocked:' above a wide dark pill bar showing '1/78' in large white bold with a thin cyan fill at the left. A green 'CLAIM ALL (4)' button appears bottom-left when several rewards are ready.

Dark panel with 'SHOP' in white bold plus a small red shopping-basket icon overhanging the top-left, and a red X overhanging the top-right. Top row: three cyan-to-blue vertical gradient cards with light blue borders, each showing cartoon blue-and-white sneaker art with thick black outlines (one pair, then a bag of sneakers, then a chest of sneakers), labelled '+50M SPEED' / '+500M SPEED' / '+1B SPEED' with the number in gold and the word in white, over a green rounded button carrying the Robux icon and price (1499 / 1999 / 2999). A green bold 'MONEY' divider follows. Bottom row: three green gradient cards with cartoon dollar-bill stacks and prices '$24,000' / '$200,000' / '$800,000'.

Dark panel with a FULL-WIDTH magenta-to-pink gradient header bar carrying a subtle diamond quilted pattern and rounded top corners; 'Trail Shop' left-aligned in white chunky bold with a black outline; a red rounded-square X overhanging the header's right edge. The body is a horizontally scrolling row of cards with a thin vertical magenta scrollbar at right and a light horizontal scrollbar beneath. Each card is a rounded rect filled with the trail's colour as a gradient with diamond quilting and a dark outline, containing: the trail name in white bold, the rarity in smaller grey text beneath, a 3D preview of the chunky blocky ribbon trail, a dark rounded stat pill reading e.g. 'x2.5 Speed' (multiplier in bright green, word in white), and a purchase row with a green cash button plus a magenta Robux button. An owned item shows a single green 'Unequip' button instead.

Grey Trail (Common, x1.5), Green Trail (Uncommon, x2, $5K / R$19), Blue Trail (Rare, x2.5, $75K / R$29), Purple Trail (Epic, x3, $1.5M / R$40), Golden Trail (Legendary, x3.5, $30M / R$79), plus Red Trail, Galaxy Trail (x5, $20M), Cosmic Trail (x7, $500B) and an Eternal tier (x10). Trails double as the game's main visual flex and as a speed multiplier.
findings.source: Frames g_020, g_021; sheet3_1 row 4, sheet3_2 row 1

findings.detail: Dark panel with 'Fuse Machine' in white bold and a red X. Subtitle 'Bring 3 same Pets to Fuse' in white, and 'Better pets give more Luck 🍀!' with the numeral in red and 'Luck' in green italic. Three slots labelled 'Empty', each a dark rounded square holding a large green '+' button. A black hopper/funnel graphic with green corner brackets sits below. Footer shows a grey 'ical 3 Pet Left' status button.

Dark panel with a green border, 'Free Gift' title and a red X. Contains a blue gem/ice-cube icon, '— LIMITED TIME —' and '10,000 SPEED!' in red and white, three social task buttons each with a small thumbnail ('Like The Game!', 'Favorite The Game!', 'Join The Community!'), and a wide green 'CLAIM!' button at the bottom.
findings.source: sheet2_1 row 2 col 6 and row 3 col 1

findings.detail: 'The Hungry Monster Has Arrived!' — a dark panel with a gold/yellow bold title, a white subtitle, and three numbered step cards (1 FIND A PARASITE, 2 FEED THE MONSTER, 3 CLAIM THE CHEST) each with a green circled numeral, a 3D preview image, a coloured step title and white body copy on a dark card with a green border. A green 'Ok!' button closes it.

Primary UI font is a heavy rounded geometric display sans in the Fredoka One / Luckiest Guy class — very thick strokes, rounded terminals, tight letter spacing, Title Case or ALL CAPS. EVERY gameplay text element carries a 2-4px pure black outline and often a soft drop shadow, prioritising legibility over the bright saturated 3D behind it. Roblox's default UI font (Builder Sans / Gotham) appears only in the native topbar and PlayerList. All large numbers use K / M / B / T abbreviations.

Panels: near-black to dark charcoal (#2A2A32 - #3A3A42), 12-16px corner radius, with either a light grey/white stroke or a gold/tan stroke, plus a drop shadow. Confirm/buy/positive: bright green (#3FC02F - #57E03A). Destructive/close/alert/unequip: red (#E03B37 - #FF3B30). Secondary/info: blue (#3FA9F5). Premium, Robux and trails: magenta-to-pink gradients (#FF3FC0 - #FF7AD9) and purple. Speed: cyan (#31C6F5) escalating to magenta at high magnitudes. Money: bright green (#3FE03F).
findings.source: Full-res frames g_007, g_020, h_012, k_069

findings.detail: Rounded rectangles with roughly 10-14px radius, a flat saturated fill, a lighter inner border inset a couple of pixels, a hard black outer outline, and a darker bottom edge that reads as a chunky 3D bevel. Close buttons are rounded SQUARES in red with a white X, positioned OVERHANGING the panel's top-right corner rather than inside it. Panel titles similarly overhang the top-left corner. Notification badges are small red circles with a white numeral.
findings.source: Full-res frames g_007, g_020, h_012, crop_equip.png

findings.detail: Rarity is communicated as a coloured word on the pet's world-space nameplate and as coloured text in the equip list. Observed: Common = light grey/silver; Uncommon = bright green; Rare = blue; Legendary = gold/yellow; Epic and above = purple/violet; Secret = teal/white. The nameplate stacks rarity word on top, pet name in white bold beneath, and income in bright green below that — all black-outlined.
findings.source: High-zoom crop crop_names.png; frames f_028, sheet4_3

findings.detail: Documented tiers from common to rarest: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, Huge, Secret, Eternal, Divine (plus 'Cosmic' used as a tier label on some pets and 'Mutated' as a cross-cutting label). Nightflame (Titan Temple, Divine) is cited as the top income pet at $3B/s; Unicorn (Cosmic) is cited as a Divine at $1B/s.
findings.source: stealaneggroblox.wiki tier-list; games.gg biomes guide; stealthygaming pet list

findings.detail: A brilliant white / warm-white vertical light COLUMN plus a diagonal lens-flare style streak shooting up and to the side, a ground-level ring of puffy white smoke, and pale chunky eggshell debris CUBES tumbling outward. Additive/Neon, very bright, roughly one second. This is the single most prominent VFX in the game.
Fusing produces a burst of multicoloured RECTANGULAR confetti particles (pink, cyan, yellow, green) around the machine, accompanied by glowing gold/orange torus rings that expand around the player.

The equipped trail is the dominant player VFX: a solid wide ribbon/beam streaming from the player straight back and downward, rendered as a chunky bar of Neon colour (grey, green, blue, purple, gold, magenta/galaxy, white/eternal) with tumbling blocky shards along its length. At high tiers it reads as a bright magenta or gold vertical column that dominates the frame.
findings.source: Frames k_041 (gold), k_088 (magenta), k_069; sheet4_2, sheet4_3

findings.detail: '+$5' / '+$24' / '+$4K' in bright green bold with a black outline spawn above each earning pet and rise then fade. Treadmill strides fire a yellow '+2/step'. Speed gains fire green '+$8 Speed'. A centred reward toast uses a rounded rect with a cyan-to-green gradient fill, a white/black outline and a white radial starburst behind it, showing an icon plus e.g. '+1B'.

findings.topic: VFX — stealing (there is NO steal beam)
findings.detail: Stealing is NOT a beam or tractor effect. It is a proximity interaction: a white/grey circular badge containing an 'E' key glyph appears at the player, a small two-line label reads 'Egg' (grey) over 'Steal' (white bold), and the target nest/egg is wrapped in a WHITE OUTLINE HIGHLIGHT (SelectionBox-style). On success the screen shows 'You stole an EGG!' in white bold. Carrying then triggers the red RUN!! banner and a red 'Drop' button at bottom-centre.

There is no strong per-rarity aura ring on pen pets. High-rarity pets and eggs carry white or coloured SPARKLE particles and a soft emissive rim only — the Cosmic egg has cyan star sparkles, and a pink Cherry Blossom pet showed white sparkle bursts. Rarity is communicated primarily through nameplate text colour and Pet Index tile colour rather than through a world-space aura.
findings.source: Frames k_088, store4.png; absence across all pen-pet frames

findings.detail: Lava uses emissive orange Neon blocks plus fire particle plumes with glow. Snow has falling snow particles. Cosmic has white star particles and purple/magenta glow wisps, with gold/amber glowing rings orbiting the guardian in marketing art. Portals render as glowing orange/red torus rings. NO footstep dust was observed anywhere.

Traps are black spiky blocky ground props. Being caught shows 'TRAPPED' in red with a seconds countdown. Trapping another player shows 'You Trapped <username>!' in red. Placement errors show red warnings such as 'Put closer to your Pen to place pets!'.

Server-wide events use a full-width WHITE horizontal strip across the middle of the screen with dark text, a giant countdown numeral (3, 2, 1) and a black wing/comet icon. Observed strings: 'ALL EGG RESET!', 'A Secret Cerberus Egg spawned in Volcano!', 'A Secret Titan Egg spawned in Prehistoric!', 'A Secret King Snake Egg spawned in Jungle!', 'A Secret Stag Egg spawned in Cherry Blossom!'.
findings.source: sheet4_1 row 6; sheet4_2 rows 2 and 5; sheet2_2

findings.detail: Entering a biome shows the zone name at top-centre in white bold with a black outline followed by a smiley emoji — e.g. 'Forest 🙂', 'Lake 🙂', 'Desert 🙂', 'Snow 🙂', 'Volcano 🙂', 'Prehistoric 🙂', 'Abyss Ocean'. Casual and low-ceremony, no banner plate.

The four Roblox store screenshots are composited marketing renders, noticeably higher fidelity than shipped gameplay: they use faceted smooth low-poly creatures (a banded orange/brown snake with a visibly triangulated head; a striped orange T-Rex), cut-out player avatars with white rim strokes, radial white speed lines on a cyan sky, red curved arrows, red '!!' marks, and headline text in a rainbow gradient chunky font with thick black and white outlines plus income figures in green ('TREX EGG', '$89,121Sp/s', 'YOU!'). A 3D artist should treat these as the aspirational target, not the shipped bar.

Yeti (Snow): white chunky voxel cubes stacked, black curved ram horns, red glowing angular eyes, open red mouth with white teeth, black claws, cyan ice crystal shards on shoulders and back. T-Rex / crocodilian (Prehistoric): sage-olive green blocky build with darker green dorsal stripes, white jaw and teeth, ~40-60 boxes, lying flat. Cosmic dragon: dark charcoal low-poly with jagged crystalline spines, magenta energy wisps and amber glowing rings, shown asleep with a blue 'Zzz'. A large red kraken/octopus is visible near the base area.
Standard Roblox third-person camera, fairly close and slightly elevated, no custom FOV shifts, no cinematic framing, no camera shake on hatch or steal events.

Active pet slots are shown as '14/14 Active' in the equip panel header, with a red '+1 EQUIP [$1T]' button to purchase an additional slot using in-game cash. Pen capacity is separately upgraded via an 'Upgrade Pen — Level 1 > Level 2 — $15K' plaque with both a cash button and a Robux option (R$19).
'You earn $334B/Day offline!' appears as an offline-earnings notification. 'Friend Boost +10%' sits bottom-left when playing with friends. Both use the same white bold black-outlined display type.

openQuestions: Settings menu contents were never opened on camera — music/SFX sliders, graphics options and a hide-other-players toggle are assumed but unconfirmed.
Titan Temple (the 7B-speed endgame zone) was only glimpsed in passing; its full palette, architecture, guardian (Gorilla King) and nest design need dedicated footage.
The two custom circular buttons in the top-left next to Roblox's unibar were never clicked; their functions (emote wheel? codes? rewards?) are unconfirmed.

Whether pen pets have a subtle idle animation could not be resolved — no walk cycle, orbit or follow behaviour was seen, but a low-amplitude idle bob may exist below the resolution of sampled frames. Worth confirming with continuous footage of a static pen.
Exact hex values are eyeballed from compressed 720p YouTube frames; sample directly from an uncompressed capture before locking a palette.
Polygon counts are silhouette-based estimates, not extracted geometry. If exact budgets matter, they would need to come from inspecting the actual Roblox assets.
The Sakura Incubator (Cherry Blossom mutation machine) and the Bloom / Spirit Bloom mutation visuals were never seen on screen — only documented in text sources.
Cosmic biome in-game (as opposed to the marketing render) was only briefly visible; the magenta ground plane and nebula sky may be marketing-only.
The 'Growing Eggs' right-side tracker panel was only seen at contact-sheet resolution; its exact row layout, typography and state pills need a full-res capture.
stealanegg.fandom.com is behind Cloudflare and could not be scraped for canonical pet/egg reference art; a manual browser visit would add per-pet model references.
